Filter types, value extraction, and the filter popup — current-state reference. See `PROJECT.md` for the node tree / memoization model these filters plug into.

## Value-extraction pattern language

A filter query is a candidate for extraction (`isExtractPattern`) the moment it contains a placeholder token — but whether it actually *becomes* an `extract` filterType now also depends on the popup's **"Extract values"** checkbox (see "Filter popup: Extract values checkbox, target chain, layout" below); with the checkbox unchecked, a wildcard pattern stays a plain `text` filter, matched via the same regex but only tested, not captured into a table. `compileExtractPattern(pattern)` turns the template into `{ regex, columns, regexStr }` — `regexStr` (the raw source string, added alongside the compiled `regex`) exists purely so the live pattern preview (see "Extraction: live pattern preview + ignored columns" below) can build its own second `RegExp` with the `d` (match-indices) flag without touching the hot-path `regex` used for actual matching; the wildcard-as-filter `text` path (see below) also reuses `regexStr` directly, just rebuilt with the case-sensitivity flag the "extract" path always hardcodes to insensitive.

Placeholders: `[*:float]` `[*:int]` `[*:time]` `[*:word]` `[*:hex]` and the bare wildcard `[*]`. `time` matches either a clock time (`16:23:27.697`) or a number+unit duration (`500ms`, `3.5s`). Columns are named after the word right before their placeholder (`deriveExtractColumnBase`: `temperature=[*:float]` → `temperature`; one trailing `=`/`:` stripped, stop words like `in`/`at`/`after` skipped, so `completed in [*:int]ms` → `completed`; case kept), falling back to `value` when there is no usable word (pattern start, `(`, a digit); duplicates get a suffix (`x`, `x 2`; `value`, `value 2`). **Tuple messages** (`deriveTupleNames`, one self-contained helper run over the pattern text before the per-token rule): a NAME LIST paired positionally with a VALUE LIST names the columns — `Probe offset (xo, yo, zo): (1.4 , 7.98, 9.76)` → `xo`/`yo`/`zo`, also `=`/`->`/`=>` connectors and `()` `[]` `{}` `<>` brackets (`[cx; cy] -> [12px; 40px]`, `{a/b}={3/4}`, `<u, v> = <1 m, 2 m>`). Value list = ≥ 2 consecutive placeholders separated only by an optional unit plus ONE separator kind (`,` `;` `/` `|` or whitespace); name list = ≥ 2 identifiers directly before it with one separator kind, in its own bracket pair (unbracketed only with `, ; / |` — a bare space-separated run of words is an ordinary sentence, `Queue depth: [*:int] [*:int]` stays `depth`/`value`; bracketed names may be space-separated: `(gx gy gz) = (1 2 3)`). Counts must match, else no pairing at all and the word-before rule applies; mixed separators inside one list also cancel it; a closing bracket after the values, if present, must be the counterpart of the opening one. Units: each placeholder's own unit (`1.4mm ,`, `1 m,`) wins over a group unit — a bracketed unit after the names (`(xo, yo) [mm]:`, `(mm)`, `{mm}`), a unit after the closing bracket (`(...) mm`), or, for an unbracketed value list, a unit on the last placeholder only (`xs, ys: 1.2, 3.4 µm`). Placeholders outside a paired list keep the word-before rule. A short unit word right after a float/int/hex placeholder (≤ 4 chars of letters/`°%µ/`, not a stop word like `and`/`per`) becomes `col.unit` (` C`, ` bar`, `ms`), shown in plot axis titles as `temperature [C]` (`columnAxisLabel`). Names are never the type string itself (that caused a "floatfloat" header rendering bug early on). A rename (`columnRenames`) replaces the name; the unit stays. Regex is case-insensitive **and dotAll** (`"is"` flags — added this session, 2026-09-04, person-reported: a `[*]`/`[*:word]`'s `.`/`.*` fragment didn't match a literal newline by default, so a pattern meant to span a multi-line message, e.g. a stack trace, silently found nothing); a trailing `[*]` is greedy (captures the rest of the line — now the rest of the *message*, newlines included), a mid-pattern `[*]` is non-greedy. Every place that recompiles this pattern's `RegExp` from `regexStr` (`textFilterMatchSpec`, `evaluateFilterCondition`'s `"text"` branch, `evaluateLiveMatch`, `updateFilterPatternPreview`) appends `"s"` too — only `compileExtractPattern`'s own `regex` carries it natively.

Right-click a message → **"Extract numbers from this message"** auto-generates a suggested pattern (`buildNumericExtractPattern`) by replacing every number token with a typed placeholder, recognizing embedded clock times/durations as a single `[*:time]` rather than splitting on the colons. A number never starts right after an ASCII letter/digit/underscore/dot, nor after `<letter>-`, so an identifier is never split into an int column (`J-00001` once became −1); instead a whole token that starts with an ASCII letter and contains a digit (`J-00004`, `worker-3`, `v2`, `gen2`, hashes like `a3f9`) becomes one `[*:word]` capture, so the pattern matches every entry of that shape, while `target=-20.6` and CJK-adjacent numbers still extract as numbers. It's inserted into the filter popup for review, not auto-submitted.

**"Filter for this ___" collapses an embedded newline into `[*]` before it ever reaches the input** (this session, 2026-09-04, person-reported follow-up to the dotAll fix above: the auto-generated pattern for a multi-line message still didn't find it). `#filterInput` is a single-line `<input type="text">` — the browser's own value-sanitization algorithm for single-line text controls silently strips any `"\r"`/`"\n"` the moment it's assigned to `.value`, so a pattern built straight from a multi-line entry's literal message text (a stack trace, a wrapped line) had its newlines dropped before the pattern was ever submitted, corrupting it. `openFilterForEntryColumn` now runs its pattern (numeric-wildcarded or literal fallback, either one) through `collapseNewlinesToWildcard()` first, replacing each `\r\n`/`\r`/`\n` run with the bare `[*]` token — which survives the input untouched and, since it now spans a newline, still matches straight through the break.

### Value conditions

`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` item 5 ("Numeric greater/less-than filter"), implemented differently than originally scoped there per explicit person instruction: not a separate filter type, but a numeric condition folded directly into a `[*:float]`/`[*:int]` placeholder, e.g. `[*:float>=10]` (single condition) or `[*:int<20,>10]` (`,`-separated conditions, AND-ed together — matches ints strictly between 10 and 20). Working through the **existing filter/extract wildcard paths only**, as requested — no new filter type, no new filter-node field (the condition lives inside the pattern string itself, `node.value`, so every persistence carrier already threads it through untouched, unlike CLAUDE.md's "Known gotchas" note on genuinely new fields).

**Same-day follow-up** (person asked whether the syntax was sensible and requested an absolute-value variant — *"größer als absolut zehn"*): the condition separator was swapped from the originally-shipped `;` to `,` (more conventional), and a condition's operator can now be prefixed with `|` to compare against the captured value's **absolute value** instead, e.g. `[*:float|>=10]` matches both `10` and `-15`. `abs` is a per-condition flag, not per-placeholder — `[*:int|>10,<=100]` mixes an abs and a plain condition on the same placeholder.

`EXTRACT_TOKEN_RE` now captures an optional condition group right inside the brackets, and `compileExtractPattern` parses it (`parseValueConditions`) onto that column as `.conditions: [{op, value, abs?}, ...]` — absent (`undefined`) for a bare placeholder, same shape as before. A condition on `time`/`word`/`hex` (no natural numeric ordering) makes the whole pattern invalid (`compileExtractPattern` returns `null`), surfacing through the exact same "Invalid pattern" feedback the popup already had for a malformed regex — no new error path. The per-condition pattern (`VALUE_CONDITION_ONE`, e.g. `\|?(?:>=|<=|==|>|<)-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?`) is a single shared string constant, built once and reused by both `EXTRACT_TOKEN_RE` (recognizing the whole conditions substring as part of a token) and `VALUE_CONDITION_RE` (re-parsing that substring into individual conditions) — the two can't drift apart into recognizing different condition syntax.

**Matching**: the regex itself is unchanged (a comparison isn't expressible as a regex quantifier) — conditions are checked as a post-match numeric step, `Math.abs()`-ing the captured value first when `.abs` is set. `wildcardMatch(regex, columns, text)` is the one shared primitive (`getEntries`'s `"extract"` branch, `textFilterMatches`' wildcard path for a plain `"text"` filter carrying wildcard tokens, and the filter popup's live-match count all call it), so extraction and the wildcard-as-filter `text` path can never disagree about what a conditioned placeholder matches.

**Visualization** ("value pills"): every place that already showed a placeholder's type visually now also shows its condition (`describeValueConditions`, e.g. `≥10`, `<20 ∧ >10`, or `|≥10` for an abs condition) — the filter popup's live pattern preview (a small `.preview-value-cond` badge next to the matched value span), the post-creation `#extractPatternView` pattern-chip, and the extraction table's column header. The pattern preview's sample-message search was also changed to require the condition to actually hold (not just a structural regex match) — before this fix it could show, say, `score=0` as the "match" for `[*:int>=10]`, which the real filter would then reject; it now walks `baseEntries` checking `valueSatisfiesConditions` alongside the regex match, same as the real filter does, and falls back to the existing "No matching sample message yet." state if no entry actually satisfies the condition. For an abs condition, this means the shown sample can legitimately be a negative value.

**Discoverability: the "Narrow" hint row** (`#filterNumberHint`, backlog #111, 2026-10-07). The syntax used to be documented only in the `[int]`/`[float]` chip tooltips, invisible on touch. Below the Insert chips, a row `Narrow [*:float]:` appears whenever the Text-syntax pattern holds an int/float token (hidden in Regex mode and otherwise). Its chips `>=10`, `<20,>10`, `|>=10`, `@en 1,234`, `@de 1.234` rewrite one token in place (`findNumberHintToken`: the token around the caret, else the last one before it, else the last one): a condition chip replaces the token's condition, a format chip its `@en`/`@de` suffix (format stays before the condition, `[*:float@de>=10]`); tapping the active (`aria-pressed`) chip removes it, and the caret lands right after the condition so the example numbers can be edited. Chips carry `data-cond` keys (`NUMBER_HINT_VALUES` maps them to the strings) because raw `<`/`>`/`|` in attribute selectors break the jsdom fast-selector check (GROUP 346). Tested by GROUP filter-number-hint.

Regression-tested: **Group 81** — `compileExtractPattern` parsing (single condition, `,`-separated multiple conditions in order, an abs-prefixed condition, a mixed abs/plain pair, the `time`/`word`/`hex` rejection, bare-placeholder backward compatibility), extraction and wildcard-as-text-filter matching against both an abs and a non-abs condition on signed data, the extraction table header + pattern-view chip visualization (including the abs `|` prefix), and the filter popup's live-match count + pattern-preview sample/badge (including the "no entry satisfies the condition" empty state and a negative-value abs sample).

## Filter popup: Extract vs. Add filter as two buttons, scope hint, sectioned layout, live results, "Filter for this ___"

(Searching without creating a node is the find bar's job — `Ctrl+F`/`F3`, see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Find bar". Its "Add as filter" makes the same `createFilterNode("text", …)` call this popup's `commitFilter` does.)

Four person-requested passes on `#filterPopup`, same week (2026-08-17: sizing/layout → a section reorg + context-menu rename, same day → a bugfix flipping a checkbox's default, same day again → the checkbox removed entirely in favor of two plain buttons — described here as the current, post-all-four-passes shape end-to-end rather than layered deltas; see "Status / changelog" below for what changed in which pass).

**Extract vs. plain filter is decided ENTIRELY by which button gets clicked — there is no other state involved.** `#filterExtractBtn` ("Extract", `type="button"`) and `#filterSubmitBtn` ("Add filter" in create mode, "Save" in edit mode, `type="submit"`) both call the same `commitFilter(asExtract)`: `asExtract === true` (the Extract button) always creates/updates an `"extract"` node; `asExtract === false` (Add filter/Save) always creates/updates a plain `"text"` node — even when its `value` happens to contain `[*:...]`/`[*]` wildcard tokens (see below). This replaced an `#filterExtractCheckbox` toggle that shipped, then was bugfixed, then was removed outright the same week, per the person's explicit design principle: *"Das Filter Edit Dialog sollte keine grundlegend unterschiedlichen Zustände kennen, sondern nur unterschied initialisiert werden. alle Zustände sind dabei im Dialog selbst visualisiert. keine versteckte Logik im Hintergrund."* A checkbox — even correctly defaulted — still leaves a checked/unchecked *state* sitting in the popup between typing and submitting; two buttons leave none, since the decision is made and consumed in the same click. `filterExtractBtn.disabled` is the only thing anything still toggles ahead of time, and it's a pure capability gate (`isExtractPattern(filterInput.value)` — is there anything to extract at all), not a decision about which outcome will happen.

**A `"text"` filter's `value` can itself contain wildcard tokens** (created by clicking "Add filter"/"Save" while the input has `[*:...]`/`[*]` in it) — `getEntries`'s `"text"` branch detects that (`isExtractPattern(node.value)`) and, instead of a literal substring `includes()`, tests a regex built from `compileExtractPattern(node.value).regexStr` (rebuilt with the right case-sensitivity flag rather than the extraction path's hardcoded `"i"`) via the same `textFilterMatches()` used everywhere else — so column-restriction, case-sensitivity, and `inverted` (NOT) all keep working normally, unlike a real `"extract"` node where NOT/case/columns are unavailable (see "Inversion (NOT)" above). No new node field: the distinction is derived purely from `filterType` + whether `value` contains tokens, so every existing persistence carrier already threads it through untouched. Because of this, NOT/case-sensitivity/column-restriction are **never** conditionally disabled or hidden by pattern content anymore (an earlier pass did this, tied to the now-removed checkbox) — they're parameters of the "Add filter" outcome only, and Extract simply never reads them, so there's nothing left to gray out based on what's typed. The one later addition that *is* content-gated, "Match whole word", is the same kind of pure capability gate `#filterExtractBtn` already was — the option has no definition at all for a regex or a wildcard pattern, so greying it out with an explaining tooltip is what keeps the state visible in the dialog instead of leaving a checked box that silently does nothing (see "Text filter: match whole word" below).

**Editing an existing filter goes through the exact same `commitFilter`.** Clicking "Save" on a node that's currently `"extract"` replaces it with a plain `"text"` filter; clicking "Extract" on a node that's currently `"text"` turns it into a real extraction — `updateFilterNode` always writes whichever type the clicked button dictates, there is no "preserve the old type" step. This is what makes both explicitly requested directions possible: editing an extraction down to a plain filter, and editing a plain filter up into an extraction.

Two spots set `#filterInput.value` directly (not via a real keystroke): `insertTokenAtCursor` (a token-chip click) and the "Filter for this ___" context-menu action (below). Both must call `updateFilterAvailability()` themselves (the shared refresher for both content-driven availability states: `updateExtractAvailability()` + `updateWholeWordAvailability()`), not just `evaluateLiveMatch()` — a plain `"input"` listener never fires for a programmatic `.value` write, and without this the Extract button could get stuck disabled (and "Match whole word" stuck enabled) after a wildcard was inserted any way other than typing it.

**Scope hint (`#filterScopeHint`, 2026-09-23)** replaced the `"Filter on:"` / `"Edit filter on:"` header row and its `#filterTargetChain` pill chain (`renderFilterTargetChain`, deleted together with the last `.crumb` CSS). `renderFilterScopeHint()` writes `in <name>` into a small tag *inside* the input's box — `.filter-input-wrap` carries the border/focus/error state (via `:has(#filterInput…)`), the `<input>` itself is borderless — naming only the direct node the filter runs against (`filterPopupBaseId`: the active node in create mode, the edited node's existing parent in edit mode), cut to its first `FILTER_SCOPE_HINT_MAX` (15) characters plus "…"; the full name is the tooltip. The close button sits right of the input. Create vs. edit is told apart by the submit button ("Add filter" / "Save").

**Layout** (reworked 2026-09-23 after a person-supplied mockup; the app's own styling kept), top to bottom: (1) `.filter-input-section` — the input row (scope hint + `#filterInput` + close) and the wildcard chips (`#filterTokenChips`: `[int]` `[float]` `[time]` `[word]` `[hex]` `[*]`); (2) `.filter-settings-row` — **Syntax**: the Text/Regex segmented switch (`#filterSyntaxText`/`#filterSyntaxRegex`), then **Match case**, **Whole word**, **Exclude (NOT)**; (3) `#filterColumnChips` — **Search in**, the column-restriction chips; (4) `#filterPatternPreview` — the wildcard pattern preview (see `docs/extraction-and-plotting.md`); (5) `#filterResults` — the live result summary; (6) `.filter-footer-row` — the submit button, right-aligned. The three captioned rows (Insert / Syntax / Search in) put their `.filter-section-label` in a fixed-width, uppercase left column so their controls line up. **Two toggle looks** (person-requested follow-ups, same day): the exclusive **Text/Regex** choice is a segmented `.view-tabs` group — `#fhTabs`' Context/Filtered/Table/Plot look. The **independent on/off options** — Match case, Whole word, Exclude (NOT), and each Search in column (`#filterColumnChipGroup`, `.column-chip` + `.active`/`aria-pressed`) — are each a standalone `.label-toggle` (in a plain `.filter-toggle-set` flex row, never boxed into a shared control): chrome-free label, `--accent-strong` when on plus a thin bar under it as the on/off status light — the same rule `.icon-toggle` follows, so a single-label toggle never reads as an action button. The three switches keep the `.pill-toggle` state protocol (`role=switch` + `aria-checked` + `.on`, `pillGet`/`pillSet`, the shared delegated click handler also matching `.label-toggle[role="switch"]`); `.label-toggle-danger` keeps NOT red; Whole word disables itself via `:disabled`. The Insert chips are actions, so they take the app's framed button look (`.toolbar-icon-btn`'s frame/fill/hover, 28px) instead. `#filterPopup` has `max-height:calc(100vh - 76px); overflow-y:auto`.

**Live result summary (`#filterResults`, `evaluateLiveMatch` → `renderLiveResults`)**, debounced 150ms, always previewing the "Add filter" outcome against `applyLevelFilter(getEntries(filterPopupBaseId))`: a big count (`.filter-live-count`) with "matches in N" (or "kept (NOT) in N") and, for a wildcard pattern, a "captures: value (int), …" line (ignored columns left out); right of it `#filterResultsMinimap`, an SVG histogram of the hits over the base rows' time span (`FILTER_MINIMAP_BUCKETS` = 60 bars scaled to the fullest bucket, hidden with no hits), colored like the timeline minimap: per bin the highest-severity hit's level wins (`levelSortRank` → `minimapLevelClass`, the `.minimap-lvl-*` fills — shared with `renderTimelineMinimap`); below, the first `FILTER_SAMPLE_ROWS` (3) hits as `.filter-sample-row`s — level bar (`lvl-*` + `.col-bar`), `HH:mm:ss.SSS`, the message with the first hit wrapped in `<mark class="filter-sample-hit">` (`appendSampleMessage`; lead-in trimmed to 30 chars when the hit sits deep in a long message; nothing marked under NOT or a column restriction without Message). Zero hits → `.warn`; an invalid regex/pattern → "Invalid regex"/"Invalid pattern" in `.error`.

**"Filter for this ___"** (row context menu, right-click a log entry) replaced the old, message-only **"Extract numbers from this message"** (`#ctxExtractNumbers` → `#ctxFilterForColumn`). `resolveContextFilterColumn(ev)` walks up from `ev.target` (the row's `"contextmenu"` listener is attached once per row, so `ev.target` is whichever inner column span the pointer actually landed on) via a generic `closest("[data-col]")` — **Custom Columns** (later session) added a `data-col` attribute to every column span the row renderers emit, including Time/Level/Message (only Thread/Location/Method carried one before), so this no longer needs a parallel `CTX_FILTER_COLUMN_CLASSES` class→key table — to find which `activeTextFilterColumns()` entry was clicked (Time/Level always present, plus the union of every currently-loaded format's own columns, plus Message if shown — see "Text filter: case-sensitive + target column" below), falling back to `"message"` for anything else (row background/gutter, a link-view pair's brace). The menu label and the resulting action both read that column: `"Filter for this " + column.label`, prefilling `#filterInput` from `entryColumnValue(entry, column.key)` and pre-selecting that column in `filterPopupColumns` (the "Applies to" chips) — reusing the exact same dynamic column list the chip feature already builds from, so the two can't drift apart. Numeric content in that column's text still becomes a `[*:...]` wildcard pattern via the unchanged `buildNumericExtractPattern`; a column with no numeric content (most Method/Thread values, or a plain-text message) falls back to the **exact literal text** instead of a "No numeric values found" no-op toast, so the action is useful there too — "find this exact line/value again." This action never decides text-filter vs. extraction itself: it just opens the popup pre-filled, and whichever button gets clicked afterward decides, same as typing the pattern by hand would.

**Menu completion (`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #78)**: `"Filter for this ___"` is now the menu's **first actionable item**, directly under the timestamp meta row's separator — it used to sit further down, past After/Before/Bookmark/Note. Right next to it sits a new **Extract** item (`#ctxExtractMessage`), a one-click version that skips the filter popup entirely and commits straight to a new filter node via the unchanged `extractMessageFilter(entry)` (the same function the `#viewBar` row-action's "Extract" button already called). It's shown only when there's actually something to extract — `openContextMenu` gates its `style.display` on the exact same check the toolbar button's own `extractActionEnabled` uses, `buildNumericExtractPattern(entryColumnValue(entry, "message")) !== null` — never a disabled/greyed item, matching how the rest of this menu hides rather than disables (Bookmark/Note for a non-real entry, Time-filter-from-selection below 2 selected rows). The menu's remaining items are unchanged in behavior, just regrouped by separators into: meta → **Filter for this ___ + Extract** → After/Before/Time filter from selection → Bookmark/Note/Add to selection → **Copy** (new, see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Log row multi-select + copy").

Regression-tested: **Group 39** covers the wildcard-as-filter matching semantics (direct `getEntries()`/`textFilterMatches()` calls — case-sensitivity, NOT, and an unaffected real `"extract"` node) and the scope hint. **Group 263** covers the 2026-09-23 redesign end to end (15-char scope hint, row captions/order, Text/Regex switch incl. edit round-trip, result summary: count, meta, captures, sample rows, histogram, NOT, zero hits). **Group 40** covers the section reorg's DOM structure/top-to-bottom order and "Filter for this ___" across three columns (message/method/thread), including the literal-text fallback. **Group 41** is the current, canonical coverage for the two-button redesign itself: the checkbox's absence from the DOM, the original person-reported repro (context-menu prefill → "Add filter" → plain `"text"` node, never a silent extraction), the same outcome for a hand-typed Ctrl+F pattern (one shared code path, not per-entry-point branching), extraction still reachable via the Extract button, and — the part a checkbox-based design structurally couldn't do — editing an *existing* extraction and clicking "Save" to turn it back into a plain filter, and editing an *existing* plain filter and clicking "Extract" to turn it into a real extraction, both directions explicitly requested. Groups 8, 24, and 35 were updated in place where they'd relied on the checkbox (NOT staying available regardless of pattern content now, per Group 8's updated note; clicking `#filterExtractBtn` directly instead of checking a box first, in Groups 24 and 35). The `max-height`/`overflow-y` sizing fix and the buttons' visual styling are pure CSS with no jsdom-observable state and are deliberately not re-tested, same "no layout engine" gap as the `#viewBar` flex-direction regression noted in "Testing approach" below. **Group 223** covers the menu completion above: reorder, the Extract item's visibility gate + outcome, and the new Copy item's selection-aware semantics. **Group 260** (Custom Columns) covers "Filter for this ___" resolving a custom column via the generic `[data-col]` walk, and the pre-selected chip reflecting a custom column too.

## Text filter: case-sensitive + target column

`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md`'s "Case-sensitive option for text filters" and "Per-filter target column", bundled into one feature (same session, 2026-08-16). Both are `text`-filter-only options (extract patterns already match via their own regex against `entry.message`, unaffected):

- **`node.caseSensitive: boolean`** (default/absent = case-insensitive, unchanged behavior). A checkbox in the filter popup, **default unchecked** as requested.
- **`node.columns: string[]`** — restricts matching to specific table columns instead of the whole raw line. **Custom Columns** (later session) generalized the option list from a fixed six to `activeTextFilterColumns()`: Time + Level (always present) + the active root file's own middle columns (`activeColumnDefs()` — Thread/Location/Method plus any custom columns, of that file's formats, same scope as the level filter bar's `activeLevelOrder()`) + Message (if any of those formats shows it). One toggle chip per column in the popup (now JS-rendered by `renderFilterColumnChipButtons()` from that dynamic list, not six static buttons), **same selection logic as the level filter bar** (`state.levelFilter`/`applyLevelFilter`): none selected searches every column (`entry.raw`, byte-identical to the pre-existing behavior), one or more restricts the search to just those — so selecting *every* chip and selecting *none* produce the identical matching result, just via different code paths (no special-casing to collapse "all" back to "none" in storage — not worth the complexity for a functionally-equivalent outcome).

Shared matching logic lives in `textFilterMatches(entry, value, caseSensitive, columns)` (used by both `getEntries`'s `"text"` branch and the filter popup's live-match preview, so the two never disagree) and `entryColumnValue(entry, key)` (the column-key → entry-field lookup — replaces the old fixed-switch `textColumnValue`; a key outside the six reserved fields reads `entry.fields[key]`, a custom column's value). Popup state: `filterCaseCheckbox` (`#filterCaseCheckbox`) and `filterPopupColumns` (a working `Set`, mirrored onto `.column-chip.active` classes via `renderFilterColumnChips()`), same create/edit/submit lifecycle as the pre-existing `filterPopupIgnored` (extract's ignored-columns set) — pre-filled from the node in edit mode, applied on submit, reset on close. `updateInvertAvailability()` (already responsible for disabling NOT on an extraction pattern) now also disables the case checkbox and hides the column chips the moment the input is detected as an extraction pattern, and clears both from the node if an existing `text` filter is edited into one.

Threaded through every persistence carrier per CLAUDE.md's "Known gotchas" note on filter-node fields: `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree` (undo/redo), `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson` (save/load JSON — `importFilterJson` validates `columns` entries against `knownTextFilterColumnKeys()`, dropping unrecognized ones from a hand-edited file), and `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters` (session cache) — same 4-touch-point pattern already established for `node.ignoredColumns`/`node.assertions`. **Custom Columns note**: `knownTextFilterColumnKeys()` is deliberately broader than `activeTextFilterColumns()` — it validates against every format `state.logFormats` knows about, not just currently-loaded ones, so a saved filter's restriction to a custom column survives even when that column's owning format isn't open right now (a genuinely unknown key, on no format at all, is still stripped).

Regression-tested (**Group 35** in `tests/philogg.regression.test.js`): `getEntries` matching semantics for each column key, the "all columns = no restriction" equivalence, case-sensitive vs. case-insensitive matching, popup defaults/live-match/chip-toggling, edit-mode pre-fill and re-save, the extract-pattern field-clearing edge case, and all four persistence carriers round-tripping both fields. **Group 260** (Custom Columns) extends this for a per-format custom column specifically: the dynamic chip list, `entryColumnValue`'s `fields` fallback, and `knownTextFilterColumnKeys()`'s "kept even when the owning format isn't loaded" persistence behavior.

## Regex filter type: "Interpret input as regex"

`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #16, implemented per the person's own stated refinement: not a separate filter type, but a per-filter syntax switch in `#filterPopup` — since 2026-09-23 the **Text / Regex** segmented control in the Syntax row (`#filterSyntaxText`/`#filterSyntaxRegex`, state = the Regex button's `.active`, read via `isFilterRegexMode()`/`setFilterRegexMode()`; previously the `#filterRegexCheckbox` "Interpret input as regex" pill). Switching to Regex sets a new `node.isRegex: boolean` on an otherwise ordinary `"text"` filter node (default/absent = the existing wildcard-token/plain-substring behavior, completely unchanged) — this is deliberately additive to the same filterType, not a fourth match-mode competing with `"text"`'s existing plain/wildcard split, since case-sensitivity and column-restriction (both `"text"`-only options already) are exactly as meaningful for a real regex as for a plain string.

**Compilation and matching**: `compileRegexFilter(source, caseSensitive)` — `new RegExp(source, caseSensitive ? "" : "i")`, wrapped in a `try/catch` returning `null` on a `SyntaxError` — is the one shared primitive `getEntries`'s `"text"`/`isRegex` branch, `textFilterMatches` (a new optional `regexObj` parameter, checked before the existing `wildcardRegex` parameter), and the popup's `evaluateLiveMatch` all go through, so the three can never disagree about what's a valid pattern or what it matches. When `regexObj` is set, `textFilterMatches` runs `regexObj.test(...)` against either the target column(s) (same `columns`/`entryColumnValue` restriction every other `"text"` mode already respects) or the whole raw line — no wildcard-token compilation, no `[*:...]` capture semantics, just a real `RegExp.test()`. An invalid regex compiles to `null` and degrades gracefully everywhere it's checked: `getEntries` returns an empty result (no throw), the popup's live-match count shows an inline `--level-error` "Invalid regex" state (the same visual language as the pre-existing "Invalid pattern" state for a malformed extraction pattern), and `commitFilter` refuses to submit, flashing `#filterInput`'s existing `input-error`-style shake animation (a parallel `input-regex-error` class/keyframe) and leaving the popup open to fix it — mirroring the extraction pattern's own "won't compile" submit guard exactly, just for a different compiler.

**UI**: `updateRegexModeUI()` toggles `#filterTokenChips`' visibility (the `[float]`/`[int]`/`[time]`/… insert chips — meaningless once the input isn't the wildcard-token language) and force-hides the live pattern preview (`#filterPatternPreview`, which only ever shows wildcard capture-group highlighting) the moment Regex is selected; every other section of the popup — case-sensitivity, NOT, the "Search in" column chips, the live match count, the scope hint — stays exactly as visible/usable as it already was, per the explicit instruction to hide/disable ONLY the wildcard-token-specific pieces. `updateExtractAvailability()` now also disables the Extract button whenever regex mode is on (a raw regex carries no `[*:...]` placeholder vocabulary for the extraction table to build columns from), regardless of what's typed. Opening the popup to edit an existing regex `"text"` node pre-selects Regex from `node.isRegex` and runs the same UI update, same as every other popup field's edit-mode pre-fill.

Threaded through every persistence carrier per CLAUDE.md's "Known gotchas" note, the same 6-touch-point pattern `caseSensitive`/`columns` already established: `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree` (undo/redo via delete), the field-edit-undo `captureNodeFields`/`applyNodeFields` carrier (in-place edits, e.g. clicking "Save" on an existing node — a 4th carrier beyond CLAUDE.md's three named ones, since `updateFilterNode` calls funnel through it too), `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson` (save/load JSON), `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters` (session cache).

Regression-tested: **Group 122** — `getEntries`/`textFilterMatches` regex semantics (real regex anchoring/case-sensitivity, column restriction, an invalid pattern degrading to an empty result without throwing), the popup's UI (chips/preview hidden, case/NOT/columns still usable, Extract disabled, live-match count, the inline "Invalid regex" state, submit refusing an invalid pattern and staying open), and all four persistence carriers (plus the field-edit-undo carrier) round-tripping `isRegex`.

## Text filter: match whole word

Person-requested (2026-09-01): `node.wholeWord: boolean` on an ordinary `"text"` filter node, **default off/absent** (unchanged behavior). `"Test"` matches `"Test is active"` and `"unit-Test done"` — a hyphen is a boundary — but not `"Testing activated"` or `"retest pending"`. Same additive shape as `caseSensitive`/`columns`/`isRegex`: no new `filterType`, no new match mode, just one more parameter of the literal search, and it combines freely with the other three.

**Matching** lives in `includesWholeWord(hay, needle)` — an `indexOf` scan that accepts an occurrence only when neither the character before it nor the character after it is a word character (`isWordChar`, which reads a position past either end of the string as `undefined`, so the string edges count as boundaries). `textFilterMatches` takes it as a trailing `wholeWord` argument and applies it in its literal branch only, both for a column-restricted search and for the whole-raw-line one.

Two deliberate choices:

- **Not a `\b`-wrapped `RegExp`.** `\b` is defined over ASCII `[A-Za-z0-9_]` only, so `"Gr"` would count as a whole word inside `"Größe"` (`ö` isn't in that class) — wrong for German log text, which is the point of the option. `WORD_CHAR_RE` is `/[\p{L}\p{N}_]/u` instead. The `u` flag is safe here because the regex is ours; wrapping a *person-typed* pattern in `\p{...}` lookarounds would have needed `u` on their regex too, which changes what some valid patterns mean.
- **Literal branch only.** A real regex (`\b`, lookarounds) and the wildcard-token language (`[*:word]`, `[*]`) both express boundaries themselves, so `evaluateFilterCondition` passes the flag only where it has a definition. To keep that from being invisible background logic, `updateWholeWordAvailability()` greys the toggle out (`#filterWholeWordRow.disabled`, plus a tooltip saying why) the moment regex mode is on or the input contains wildcard tokens — driven by the same `"input"` listener and regex-mode `change` that already drive the Extract button, via the shared `updateFilterAvailability()` — and `commitFilter` refuses to store the flag on such a node at all, so a node never carries a field that does nothing in the carriers it travels through.

**Match highlighting** honours it too: `textFilterMatchSpec` puts `wholeWord` on the spec (always `false` for the regex/wildcard specs, matching the rule above), and `findMatchRanges` skips an occurrence glued to a word character — so a marked span is always a span the filter itself accepted.

Threaded through every persistence carrier per CLAUDE.md's "Known gotchas", the same touch points `isRegex` established: `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, the field-edit-undo `captureNodeFields`/`applyNodeFields`, `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`, `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`, plus `bakeNodeCondition`/`getEntriesFromBaked` (and its `materializeBaked` inverse) so an AND/OR/LINK side keeps the flag it was baked with.

Regression-tested: **Group 149** — matching semantics (default off, hyphen-as-boundary, the Unicode `"Größe"` case, combination with case-sensitivity/column-restriction/column-less search), an AND over a whole-word side, highlight ranges, the popup (default unchecked, live-match count, greying out for wildcard and regex input, submit not storing the flag for a regex, edit-mode pre-fill and clearing), all persistence carriers, and the switch-style markup of all four popup toggles.

## Entry-set filter: `"idset"`

An explicit, pre-computed match set — `node.value: string[]`, an array of entry ids — matched via a plain `Set` lookup in `getEntries` (`parentEntries.filter(e => idSet.has(e.id))`). The same "second, non-rule-based source of truth" shape `"timerange"` and the auto-managed `"bookmarks"` node already use, but generic and person-creatable (unlike `"bookmarks"`, which is a singleton auto-synced from `state.bookmarks`) — built for "Create a filter from the plot view"'s part (b) below, but not itself plot-specific: anything that can name an exact set of entry ids can produce one. `idSetFilterName(ids)` names the node by count ("N entries (plot view)") since the ids alone don't say *why* they were picked — the framing lives in whichever UI action created it. No dedicated edit UI (same tier as `"and"`/`"or"`/`"link"`/`"level"` — the tree context menu's "Edit filter…" stays gated to `"text"`/`"extract"`/time-filter types).

**No new persistence-carrier code needed** — like `"timerange"`, its value rides the existing generic `node.value` field every carrier (`cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`, `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`) already copies/serializes for every filter type — this is the same "the gotcha doesn't apply here" case `"timerange"`'s own writeup documents, verified directly (not just assumed) via a real `cloneSubtree` copy/paste round trip in Group 123.

## "Create a filter from the plot view" (FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #11)

Resolves the backlog item's own stated open question — "which of the two (time-range vs. exact-entries), or both" — by implementing **both**, off the Plot tab's own zoomed/panned viewport (see "Plot zoom/pan" in `docs/extraction-and-plotting.md` for the zoom mechanism this reads from). **Rewritten 2026-09-07 (person-requested — unify the Table/Plot filters):** originally two dedicated buttons in `#plotToolbar`; now the same unified row-actions every tab uses (see "Filter-Toolbar" in `docs/ui-and-views.md`):

- **"Time range"** (`#viewBar`, `[data-row-action="timeRangeFromSelection"]`) creates a `"timerange"` filter (see "Time filters" above — the existing, generic time-range node, reused rather than inventing a new one) spanning the min/max timestamp of whatever's currently visible in the plot.
- **"Select"** (`#plotToolbar`'s own Actions group, `[data-row-action="addToSelection"]`) builds a selection filter from exactly those entries — not just their time span, but the specific rows — via the same `"idset"`-backed selection mechanism described under "Add to selection" below, rather than a dedicated one-off `"idset"` button.

Both act on the extraction node currently active, narrowing its own result further via a new child node — the same tree position a hand-built time filter under an extraction would occupy — and both are enabled only once something is actually plotted in 2D.

**"Currently visible" = the Plot tab's own zoomed/panned viewport**, not the whole extraction result — `getPlotViewportEntries()` reads `plotLastRender`'s `xDomainMin`/`xDomainMax` (the home/un-zoomed domain when no zoom is active, so clicking either action with no zoom applied naturally covers the full extraction) and, for each `extractRowsData` row, derives its X position the *exact same way* `renderPlotChart` itself positions marks — a bar chart's categorical row-index slot center (`r + 0.5`), or the X column's own `parseValueForPlot`-parsed value for line/scatter — so this can never disagree with what's actually drawn on screen. A viewport with fewer than two entries visible (e.g. zoomed into a genuine data gap) shows a toast and creates no "Time range" filter, rather than a broken empty one — "Select" only needs one.

Regression-tested: **Group 123** — the `"idset"` `getEntries` branch and its `cloneSubtree` round trip directly, the unified "Time range" action under the home (un-zoomed) view creating a filter that spans the WHOLE extraction, the same action under a real zoomed viewport creating a filter scoped to exactly the rows visible there, and the sub-2-entries no-op case; **Group 183c** covers "Select" building a selection filter from the Plot viewport.

## "Add to selection" — top-level, named, deletable `"idset"` selection filters

Turns the right-clicked log row — or the whole current multi-selection (`state.logMultiSelect`, see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Row multi-select + copy") when 2+ rows are selected — into (or *into an existing*) `"idset"` filter node (above) matching exactly those entries. Reuses the same generic entry-set filter type "create a filter from the plot view" introduced, rather than a second, parallel type.

Redesigned this session (person request) from the original single-item "Filter from selection" (which created a plain, nested-under-`state.activeId` `idset` node from a 2+ row multi-selection only). The person's framing: a selection is independent of whatever filters happen to sit above it in the tree, so it belongs at the **top level**, directly under the file — the same place the auto-managed "Bookmarks" node lives (`syncBookmarksFilterNode`, see "Bookmarks rework" in `PROJECT.md`) — not nested wherever the tree's active node happens to be.

**Marker field**: a selection filter is an `"idset"` node with `node.selectionFilter === true` — a new field needed because `"idset"` is shared with the plot-view producer above, whose nodes must NOT be treated as person-managed selections (excluded from the submenu below, from `selectionFilterNodesForRoot`, from everything this feature does).

**Placement**: `createSelectionFilterNode(rootId, ids)` always creates the node as a new, top-level child of the entry's root FILE node — `root.children.unshift(node.id)`, the exact same "top-level, unshifted so it stays near the top" placement `syncBookmarksFilterNode` uses for Bookmarks — never as a child of `state.activeId` like every other context-menu filter action.

**UI**: the log row right-click menu (`#contextMenu`) has `#ctxAddToSelection` ("Add to selection"), a submenu trigger next to "Filter for this ___", plus the "Select" toolbar action (`[data-row-action="addToSelection"]` — duplicated into `#contextToolbar`/`#filteredToolbar`/`#tableToolbar`/`#plotToolbar`, see "Filter-Toolbar" in `docs/ui-and-views.md`). Both open `#addToSelectionMenu` (built on demand, same "assemble innerHTML from data" shape `#treeContextMenu` already uses), listing every existing top-level selection filter under the entry's root file by name (`selectionFilterNodesForRoot`) — clicking one calls `addRowsToSelectionFilter(nodeId, ids)`, which appends the current row(s)' ids to that node's `value` array, deduped, without touching its name (a person may have renamed it). Below a separator, "Create new selection filter" calls `createSelectionFilterNode` instead. With zero existing selections, the submenu just shows the create entry — no empty/broken list. The current row(s) resolve per view (`currentSelectionRowIds()`, a thin wrapper around `selectActionEntries()` — see "Filter-Toolbar" in `docs/ui-and-views.md`): the right-clicked entry or the full `state.logMultiSelect` when 2+ rows are multi-selected in the log views (unlike the original, a *single* selected/right-clicked row now qualifies too), rows with at least one marked cell in Table (2026-09-07, person-requested — a partial row counts as the whole row), or the Plot tab's currently-visible viewport (`getPlotViewportEntries()`, same primitive "Time range" reads).

**Story export**: a selection filter can be quoted in a ticket as a small "story" — its name as heading, "N hand-picked entries", the entries in one block with your notes inline and gap markers. Tree context menu → **Copy for ticket** (works on a node that isn't active), or Export / Share while it is active (Lines defaults to All; the level quick filter is ignored for it). See `docs/export.md`.

**Naming**: auto-named via `nextSelectionFilterOrdinal()` at creation — a plain ordinal, "Selection 1", "Selection 2", ... (counted across every `selectionFilter` node in the tree, not per-root-file) — no dedicated naming prompt exists anywhere else in the filter tree either (every filter node is auto-named, then optionally renamed via the tree context menu's "Rename…", the same standard path a selection filter uses too). **Pointer events, touch (2026-10-03).** The drag runs on `pointerdown` (+ `setPointerCapture`) / window `pointermove`/`pointerup`/`pointercancel`, so mouse, touch and pen behave alike; `touch-action:pan-y` on the svg lets a vertical swipe scroll while a horizontal one selects (the browser's pan arrives as `pointercancel`, which aborts without creating a filter). Touch uses an 8px drag threshold (`MINIMAP_TOUCH_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX`). A touch **long-press** (500ms, finger within 10px; also reachable via the global long-press helper's synthetic `contextmenu`) opens the same time-range dialog as right-click, once per press (`fireMinimapLongPress`); the trailing click is a no-op. GROUP tablet-touch-input.

**Bugfix, this session, 2026-08-28, person-reported**: originally named via `idSetFilterName(ids, "selection")` ("N entries (selection)"), a one-time snapshot of the selection's size at creation — `addRowsToSelectionFilter` deliberately never rewrites `node.name` afterward (a person may have renamed it), so growing a selection kept its stale initial-count name forever. The plot-view producer's own `"idset"` nodes (no `selectionFilter` flag) are unaffected and still use `idSetFilterName`'s count-based name.

**Differences from Bookmarks** (all deliberate, person-specified): a selection filter is **not** `locked` — it's deletable through the normal filter-node delete action (✕ button, middle-click, tree context menu, Delete key), unlike the auto-managed, undeletable Bookmarks node. There is **no "always show" toggle** — the app's only such control, `#btnPinBookmarks` ("Pin bookmarks into Filtered View", `state.pinBookmarksInFilteredView`), is hard-wired to `state.bookmarks` specifically; nothing analogous reads or affects selection filters. And **entries added to a selection are never bookmarked** — `state.bookmarks` is never touched by any of this; membership lives purely in the idset node's own `value` array.

**Persistence**: `selectionFilter` is a genuinely new field (unlike `idset`'s shared `value`/`getEntries`, which needed no new carrier code) — threaded through `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`, and `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`, verified directly in the regression group rather than assumed.

Regression-tested: **Group 124** — a single right-clicked row (no multi-selection) creating a selection filter, top-level placement regardless of `state.activeId`, not `locked` and deletable via `deleteFilterNodeWithUndo`, never touching `state.bookmarks`, the submenu listing existing selections by name and adding a 3-row multi-selection into an existing one (deduped, including a redundant re-add), a plot-view-created `idset` node (no `selectionFilter` flag) staying excluded from the submenu, and the `cloneSubtree`/`serializeFilterTreeForCache`+`materializeCachedFilters` round trips for the new `selectionFilter` field.

## Text-filter match highlighting

Lighter alternative to `FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #13's "why is this row here" popup idea (that entry is left as-is, still unimplemented, per explicit person instruction — this feature was requested as a separate implementation, not a replacement). Marks the exact substring an active `text` filter node matched, inline in the Filter view's rows and/or the entry-detail panel, instead of requiring a click to find out why a row is present.

Runtime-only/derived — no new filter-node field, so none of the "Known gotchas" persistence carriers (CLAUDE.md) need touching. Core pieces, all just above `textFilterMatches` in `philogg.html`:

- **`getTextMatchHighlightNodes()`** — which `text` filter node(s) to pull matches from right now. Gated first by the master on/off, `textMatchHighlightEnabled` (`localStorage["philogg-text-match-highlight-enabled"]`, **default `true`**) — a **view-bar toggle button**, `#btnTextMatchHighlight` (next to `#btnPinBookmarks`/`#btnMultilineMsg`/`#btnColumns`, same plain-persistent-toggle shape — moved out of Settings same-day, person-requested: reached for while looking at the view, not an app preference). When on, `textMatchHighlightScope` (`"last"` / `"any"`, `localStorage["philogg-text-match-highlight-scope"]`, **default `"last"`**, a Settings → Behavior dropdown) picks which nodes: `"last"` = only `state.activeId` itself, and only if it IS a `text` filter — **deliberately no fallback** to a text-filter ancestor if the active node is some other type (an explicit person decision when this was scoped, not an oversight); `"any"` = every `text` filter node in the active node's own ancestor chain (`getChain`), root to active.
- **`textFilterMatchSpec(node)`** — mirrors the compilation `getEntries`'s `"text"` branch performs, in the same precedence: `isRegex` first, then a wildcard/value-token pattern, then a plain substring. Recomputed fresh per render call (not cached on the node) so an in-place filter edit (`updateFilterNode`/`applyNodeFields`) can never leave a stale spec behind. **The `isRegex` branch is new (2026-08-30)** — without it a regex node fell through to the plain-substring path and searched its own pattern *source* as a literal, which is almost never present in the log, so a regex filter that matched rows perfectly well silently marked nothing inside them. Found while extending this machinery to highlight rules (below), which would otherwise have inherited the same no-op.
- **`findMatchRanges(text, spec)`** — every `[start,end)` occurrence (not just the first) of a plain substring; for a wildcard/value-token pattern, every regex occurrence that also satisfies its numeric conditions (re-running `valueSatisfiesConditions` per occurrence, since a structurally-matching span can still fail e.g. `[*:float>=10]`); for a real regex node, every match of the compiled `RegExp`, skipping zero-width ones (a pattern like `a*` matches the empty string at every position, which would otherwise pepper the field with empty `<mark>` elements).
- **`textMatchTargetColumns(node)`** / **`matchRangesFor(text, columnKey, nodes, specs)`** — a filter's own target-column restriction (see "Text filter: case-sensitive + target column" above) decides which displayed column(s) get marked; a column-less filter (which searches the whole raw line) has no single on-screen counterpart once the raw tab-separated line is thrown away, so every displayed column is searched independently. Match ranges are searched against whichever text is actually **on screen** for a field (`formatTime(e.ts)`, ...) rather than the raw value the filter engine itself tests (`e.tsRaw` — see `entryColumnValue`); the two can diverge for "time" (the location is shown exactly as stored), so searching the displayed text keeps the marked span trivially correct at the cost of occasionally under/over-marking that column relative to the literal underlying match — an accepted, cosmetic-only trade-off.
- **`markRangesHtml(text, ranges)`** — wraps each range in `<mark class="text-match-mark">`, `escapeHtml`-ing every other slice (log content is never trusted as markup). Styled via `color-mix(in srgb, var(--warn) 55%, transparent)`, theme-consistent without a hardcoded color.

Every node's own match test is **re-run per entry**, not "trust the chain already filtered this in" — specifically so `or`/`link` nodes elsewhere in the tree (whose entries can reach a view without having passed every linear ancestor) never produce a highlight for text that isn't actually present in that particular entry.

Two independent "where" toggles, `textMatchHighlightInRows` (`renderVisibleRows`) / `textMatchHighlightInDetail` (`updateDetailPanel`), both `localStorage`-backed and **default ON**. Both these and `textMatchHighlightScope` are a **standing preference, always visible and editable in Settings → Behavior regardless of the master button's on/off state** — an explicit same-day follow-up request: the button is just a quick flip over whatever's configured there, Settings must never depend on it (an earlier version of this feature hid those rows while the button was off; that dependency was removed outright, not just relaxed). `renderVisibleRows` computes the active match nodes/specs once per render call (not per row) and reuses them across the virtualized row loop; `updateDetailPanel` does the same per selection change, and falls back to its original plain `textContent` assignment (not `innerHTML`) whenever there's nothing to mark, preserving the pre-existing "message can never be interpreted as markup" guarantee for the common case.

`tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 93 (new, revised twice same-day: first for the button move, then to drop the settings-row hide/show dependency on it): master button defaults/click-toggle/persistence, and explicit assertions that the scope select and both "where" checkboxes stay visible, enabled, and changeable while the master button is off. 1766 passed, 0 failed.

### Highlight-rule match text (`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #20)

The same inline substring marking, driven by **highlight rules** instead of the active filter path — and it is a genuinely separate feature riding shared machinery, not a mode of the one above. The two answer different questions: "why is this row in my filtered view" versus "where does each pattern I'm tracking sit", and the second one is the whole point of the Full view, where the first one doesn't apply at all.

- **Which nodes** — `getHighlightMatchNodes()`: every filter node with a `highlightColor` under the **active root file**, wherever it sits in the tree, narrowed to `filterType: "text"`. That's `computeHighlightMap`'s own node set minus the types with no substring to mark (a `level`/time/`idset`/`and`/`or`/`link` rule matches whole entries, not a span of characters). Deliberately **not** scoped to the active filter path the way `getTextMatchHighlightNodes()` is — a highlight rule is a standing "track this across the whole file" marker, which is exactly why its gutter markers already show in both views.
- **How it paints** — each rule's own colour as a **2px underline stripe** in a single shared lane. A stripe rather than a second background colour is what makes a priority rule unnecessary: one character can carry the filter path's background `<mark>` **and** any number of rule colours at once, so neither has to win — the same reasoning that already gives a multi-rule row several thin gutter markers instead of one blended colour.
  - **One lane, never stacked** (revised 2026-08-30 after the first version shipped). The lane's depth is fixed, so a rule's line runs dead straight through a region another rule overlaps. Where rules *do* overlap, the lane alternates between their colours in 5px slices (`hlStripeGradient` → `repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, …)`), which costs no vertical room and works for any number of simultaneous rules. The first version instead stacked one stripe per rule at 2px/4px/… and took each stripe's depth from the rule count of the **segment** it was in — so the very same rule sat at 2px beside a word and at 4px under it, and its line visibly stepped down mid-sentence. Depth is a property of the lane, never of the segment.
  - **Drawn inside the mark's own box**, as a `background-image` pinned to `left bottom` at `100% 2px` — never as a `box-shadow`/`padding-bottom` beneath it. That is load-bearing, not a style preference: `.row-grid` is `align-items:center`, so every log-row cell is exactly as tall as its text line box, and `.col-time`/`.col-msg`/… are `overflow:hidden`. Anything drawn under the text is clipped away and simply never appears in either log view — which is exactly what happened to the first version's stripes. Inline padding doesn't grow the line box either, so `padding-bottom` would push the stripe straight back into the clipped zone; the lane has to live inside the text's own box.
  - **Seamless joins**: one rule's underline is routinely cut into several `<mark>`s by another rule's boundary, so every mark the segmenting path emits also carries `.mark-seg`, which drops the rounded corners a standalone `.text-match-mark` has. Otherwise each piece would round its own ends and notch the join.
  - **Marking never shifts layout — fixed at its source, `mark.text-match-mark`'s own `padding`.** That rule used to carry `padding:0 1px` for a little visual breathing room — layout-affecting on an inline element, unlike background/box-shadow: side padding on `<mark>` actually widens the line, by 2px per matched run. Whether a filter match rendered through `markCombinedHtml`'s `.mark-seg` path (which zeroed padding) or fell back to plain `markRangesHtml` (which didn't) depended on whether a coloured highlight rule *also* happened to match the same field — so **toggling `#btnHighlightMatchText` visibly reflowed text nowhere near any highlight rule**, purely because it changed which path an unrelated filter match took (person-reported, 2026-08-30, pixel-compared screenshots with the button on vs. off). Fixed at the root: `mark.text-match-mark` now carries `padding:0` unconditionally, so a filter match's on-screen width is identical on every code path, whether or not any highlight rule is active.
- **How the two range lists combine** — they are never merged (`mergeMatchRanges` would destroy the per-rule colour). `markCombinedHtml(text, ranges, hlRanges)` cuts the text at every boundary either list contributes and asks both lists what applies to each resulting segment: a segment inside a filter-path range keeps `class="text-match-mark"`, one with only rule colours gets `class="hl-match-mark"` (transparent background, stripe only), and one with both keeps the background class and gains the stripe. With no rule ranges at all it delegates straight to `markRangesHtml`, so the pre-existing hot path is byte-for-byte what it was. A rule colour reaches the inline `style` attribute via `escapeHtml` — `node.highlightColor` can carry arbitrary text from a hand-edited or imported filter file, and is treated as data, not CSS.
- **Where** — all three surfaces: the Filtered view (`renderVisibleRows`), the **Full view** (`renderHighlightVisibleRows`, which the filter-path marking deliberately skips — that view is filter-path-independent by design, so the active filter's matches would be marking text in rows it makes no claim about), and the entry-detail panel. `buildMatchMarkContext(includeFilterMatches)` is the once-per-render bundle all three build and reuse across every row/field; `markFieldHtml(mm, text, columnKey)` is the single per-field entry point, short-circuiting to a plain `escapeHtml` before any range search when nothing can contribute a mark.
- **Control surface** — one view-bar toggle, `#btnHighlightMatchText` (`highlightMatchTextEnabled`, `localStorage["philogg-highlight-match-text"]`, **default `true`**), next to `#btnTextMatchHighlight` and the same plain-persistent-toggle tier. Person-chosen over the two alternatives the backlog entry itself weighed: a per-node toggle in the colour picker (would have meant a new filter-node field threaded through every persistence carrier, for a question already answered by whether the filter carries a colour at all) and a Settings checkbox. No Settings rows of its own for the same reason: *which* nodes contribute is decided by which filters are coloured, and *where* is all three surfaces unconditionally, since a highlight rule is file-wide by definition. The two buttons are fully independent — turning one off leaves the other's marks untouched.

Runtime-only again: `highlightColor` already existed and already travels through every persistence carrier, so nothing new needed threading.

Regression-tested: **Group 137** — defaults and the button's own persistence/re-init; the node set (coloured text filters outside the active chain in, uncoloured and coloured non-`text` nodes out); a rule stripe in the Filtered view, the Full view and the detail panel; the Full view carrying rule marks but never the filter path's; the detail panel carrying rule marks even with the filter path's own "show in entry detail" toggle off; two rules over the same characters sharing one alternating lane at the same depth as a single-rule run right beside it (the anti-regression for the stepping-down bug), no `box-shadow`/`padding-bottom` anywhere (the anti-regression for the clipped-stripe bug), and `mark.text-match-mark`'s own stylesheet rule declaring `padding:0` unconditionally rather than the old layout-shifting `padding:0 1px` (the anti-regression for the text-reflow bug); a span matched by both the active filter and a rule keeping the background class *and* gaining the stripe; the button gating rules only; and the `isRegex` fix (a real `RegExp` in the spec, its actual match marked rather than the literal pattern text, an invalid pattern yielding a null spec instead of throwing, and a coloured regex rule striping its real match). 2618 passed, 0 failed.

## Link filter: nearest-neighbor pairing

Built for the "give me the last position reading before each offset-computed event" use case. `getEntries` for a `link` node walks its reference-side entries and, for each one, binary-searches (`lowerBoundByTs`) the target side for the Nth entry strictly before/after it in time (`findNthOccurrence`); references with no match are dropped (no placeholder rows), duplicates are allowed. Each match becomes a **pair entry** (`buildPairEntry`) that **duck-types as a normal entry** — same `id`/`ts`/`level`/`message`/`raw` fields — specifically so every other mechanism (text/time filters, the level quick-filter, and crucially the extraction engine) works on link results completely unchanged. The two real underlying entries are combined into `message`/`raw` with the separator `PAIR_SEPARATOR = " ⟶ "`, which is why an extraction pattern spanning both sides of a pair looks like:

```
Position x=[*:float] y=[*:float] ⟶ Offset computed: [*:float]
```

A pair entry's `raw` is **not** a clean concatenation the way `message` is — it's the two source entries' full raw (tab-separated) lines with metadata in between, so it's non-contiguous and a pattern spanning the `⟶` separator can't match it the way it matches `message`. **Bugfix, this session, person-reported**: a `filterType: "extract"` node and a `filterType: "text"` node holding the *identical* wildcard/extract-token pattern gave different results on link-derived pairs — Extract always found the value table, Save (`"text"`) found nothing. `getEntries()`'s `"extract"` branch always tested `wildcardMatch(spec.regex, spec.columns, e.message)`, but `textFilterMatches()`'s own wildcard-as-text branch (a `"text"` node whose value contains extract tokens, authored via "Add filter" rather than "Extract" — see `isExtractPattern`) defaulted to `e.raw` when no column restriction was set. Fixed to default to `e.message` there too, matching the extract branch. See `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 134.

### Chained links (multi-hop tuples) — design, bugs fixed, and the new dialog

A "chained link" is a `link` node whose reference side was baked FROM another `link` node — building it by hand (link A→B, then link (A→B)→C, passing the first link's node id to `createLinkNode` as the second link's reference at creation time) still works exactly the same way, and it's also what the multi-hop dialog below generates under the hood. Since the `bakedA`/`bakedB` correction (see "Self-contained AND/OR/LINK" above), what actually gets stored is different: baking a `link` node (via `bakeNodeCondition`) copies its own `filterType: "link"` plus its `bakedA`/`bakedB`/`linkDirection`/`linkN`/etc. as a **nested baked predicate-pair**, not a reference to its node id — so "chained" here means "one link node's own baked condition nested inside another's `bakedA`/`bakedB`," evaluated recursively by `evaluateFilterCondition` (through `getEntriesFromBaked`). Three bugs in the underlying pairing mechanism were fixed in an earlier session (see `REQUIREMENTS-link-chaining-and-multiway.md`, supplied by the person, for the original repros):

- **Wrong time anchor when chaining.** `buildPairEntry(refEntry, targetEntry)` now stamps a second field, `matchTs: targetEntry.ts` — the actual matched entry's own timestamp — alongside the existing `ts` (still `refEntry.ts`, unchanged, since BASELINE anchor semantics and the display-facing pair timestamp weren't part of the bug and nothing asked for them to change). `getEntries()`'s `link` branch now searches from `refEntry.matchTs ?? refEntry.ts` instead of always `refEntry.ts`, so a second hop anchors on the *previous hop's actual match*, not the original outer reference's timestamp. A plain, non-chained `link` node is unaffected (a real entry has no `matchTs`, so this falls back to its own `.ts` exactly as before).
- **Highlighting stopped at one nesting level.** `computeHighlightMap()`'s `link` branch used to colour `pair.first.id`/`pair.second.id` directly — correct only when both sides happen to be real entries. It now calls `getTupleEntries(pair)` (below) and colours every id that comes back, so a coloured rule on a chained link colours every real entry at every nesting level.
- **Double-click jump broke on the nested side.** Same root cause, UI-facing symptom: `buildPairRow`/`revealInHighlightView` need a *real* entry id to resolve through `entryIndex`. `renderLinkView` now also flattens via `getTupleEntries(pair)` and renders one row per real entry (with `N-1` `Δ` labels between them) instead of always exactly two rows via `pair.first`/`pair.second` — so a 3+-way tuple gets a 3+-row `pair-block` in the Link view for free, and every row's double-click always has a real id.

**`getTupleEntries(entryLike)`** is the fix's shared primitive: `entryLike.isPair ? getTupleEntries(entryLike.first).concat(getTupleEntries(entryLike.second)) : [entryLike]` — recurses through arbitrarily many nesting levels instead of assuming exactly one. This is the "proposed (not mandatory) helper contract" from the requirements doc, kept as the actual implementation shape.

**Design direction chosen: A ("fix the nesting, keep pair-of-pairs"), not B ("native flat tuple").** The requirements doc offered two directions; A was chosen because it's the smaller, lower-risk diff — a chained/multi-hop tuple is still just a `link` whose own reference side is another link's baked condition (`bakeNodeCondition` nests it, `getEntriesFromBaked` recurses into it), not a new node shape. The cost is that consumers which used to assume "exactly one level of `.first`/`.second`" needed to switch to `getTupleEntries()` instead (three call sites: `computeHighlightMap`, `renderLinkView`, and nothing else touches `pair.first`/`pair.second` directly) — a small, closed set, which is what made A viable here. Direction B (a flat `entries: [...]` array + one `buildTupleEntry`) would have removed the "one level of nesting" assumption at its source rather than patching each consumer, but was judged not worth the larger diff (new node shape, new serialization fields, `and`/`or`'s and the extraction engine's `⟶`-joining logic would all need re-auditing against the new shape) for what direction A already delivers correctly.

### The link dialog: entry points, sides, steps, edit

One dialog (`#linkDialog`, "Link events" / "Edit link") creates and edits every link. `openLinkDialog(spec)` takes `{rootId, start, hops, direction, key, dt, exclusive, orderEnforced, editNodeId}`; a side is `{text}` (a pattern, baked with `bakedTextCondition` → a `text` condition on the Message column), `{nodeId}` (an existing filter, baked with `bakeNodeCondition` at Create) or `{baked}` (edit mode); a hop may carry its own `direction`/`n`. Entry points (usability round B, 2026-10-04 — testers could not find the old multi-select-only path):

- **Row context menu → "Pair with…"** (`#ctxPairWith`, real rows only, not a link-view brace): pick mode, see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Pair with… pick mode". Its "Pair all like these…" opens the dialog with both rows' message patterns (`buildNumericExtractPattern`) and the direction from the two rows' order.
- **Filter popup footer → "Link two events…"**: the popup's current text becomes Start.
- **Tree context menu / sidebar toolbar → "Link with…"** on a bakeable filter (`isLinkBakeableNode`, `openLinkWithNode`): that filter is Start, End is empty and focused.
- **Multi-selection → "Link…"** (`describeBulkActions`, 2+ filters of one file): `linkSpecFromNodeIds` makes the first selected filter Start and the rest End steps, in selection order.
- **"Edit link…"** (tree menu, toolbar, `editFilterNode`, so F2/double-click too): `linkSpecFromNode` decomposes the node with `linkChainToHops`.

Layout: **Start** row (text field + "▾"), then per step the sentence "for each start, find the [N]st [next | previous] end" (segmented control, default **next** = `after`) and an **End** row; "+ Add step" appends a step (a multi-hop tuple, each step relative to the previous match). "▾" opens a small menu of the root file's bakeable filters plus "Type a pattern"; a picked filter, or in edit mode any baked side that is not a plain `bakedTextCondition`, shows as a read-only chip named by `bakedConditionName`. A renamed filter's `node.label` is copied into the baked condition (`baked.label`, by `bakeNodeCondition`), so the chip, the link's auto-name and Unpack (`materializeBakedAsNode` gives the node its `label` back) use the custom name; a labelled baked side is never shown as a plain text field (`isPlainTextBaked`). Matching ignores the label; `baked` is copied as plain JSON by every carrier, so it survives filter file, library, session export and cache. Below: the **Same** chips (correlation key, next section), "Show only pairs with Δt" (Δt condition, below), "More options" (Don't reuse an end event, Enforce order) and the live preview.

**Create builds one node for the whole chain**: `hopsToLinkChain(start, hops, opts)` nests each step's link as the next step's `bakedA` (key and flags on every step, Δt on the last only — the shape `bakeNodeCondition` produces for a hand-chained link, see "Chained links" above), and `createLinkNodeFromBaked` places it as a new top-level child of the root file (placement rule above) and names it `linkChainName` + `linkOptionsNameSuffix` (e.g. `“A” → “B” [same job=[*:word]]`). Intermediate steps are no longer separate nodes. **Save** (edit mode) runs `updateLinkNodeWithUndo(nodeId, chain)`: one undo step (`withFieldEditUndo`, the link fields ride in `captureLinkFields`), subtree caches invalidated, and the name regenerated only while it still equals the auto-generated one, so a renamed link keeps its name.

### Opt-in options: order enforcement & exclusive matches

Both are per-`link`-node boolean flags (`linkOrderEnforced`, `linkExclusive`), set via the two checkboxes in `#linkDialog`, **default `false`** (unchanged behavior when off) — carried through `createLinkNode`'s new optional 5th `opts` argument (`{orderEnforced, exclusive}`), and persisted alongside `linkDirection`/`linkN` everywhere that already serialized those: `cloneSubtree` (copy/paste), `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree` (undo/redo), `serializeFilterBranch`'s `serializeSubtree` + `importFilterJson`'s `materialize` (filter save/load `.json`), and `serializeFilterTreeForCache`'s `ser` + `materializeCachedFilters`'s `materialize` (session cache). Additive-only fields, so `FILTER_FILE_VERSION` was **not** bumped — a filter file saved before this feature loads exactly as it did before (both new fields simply materialize `false`), and files saved with them set load correctly on older... well, there is no older-version reader to worry about going forward, but the point is nothing about the existing format 2 envelope changed.

- **Exclusive matches** (`linkExclusive`): once a target entry has been matched for one reference entry, no later reference entry in the *same node's* result can reuse it — implemented as `findNthOccurrenceExcluding()` (a variant of `findNthOccurrence` that skips ids in a running `usedIds` set) plus a `usedIds` `Set` scoped to one `getEntries()` call. **Scope chosen: globally across every tuple the node produces** (not per-hop-within-a-tuple) — the requirements doc flagged this as the more likely reading of the request and asked for it to be confirmed; going with it here since a chained/multi-hop tuple is still evaluated one `link` node at a time (each with its own `getEntries()` call and its own `usedIds`), so "global" here means "across this one node's reference entries," which is the natural unit exclusivity would apply to.
- **Enforce chronological order** (`linkOrderEnforced`): after a hop finds a candidate match, the match is **rejected (treated as no match, same as an unmatched reference — dropped, not retried)** if `match.ts < anchorTs` (the timestamp the hop searched from — the previous hop's `matchTs`, or the outer reference's own `ts` for the first hop). **Semantics chosen**: this makes the *whole chain's* timestamps non-decreasing hop-over-hop, regardless of which individual hop searched "before" vs "after" — chosen over the other candidate reading ("each hop's own direction is internally consistent") because it's the one that actually catches the requirements doc's own REPRO case (a "before" hop landing chronologically earlier than the very first reference entry, not just earlier than its immediate anchor) and because pairwise-adjacent monotonicity is transitively equivalent to whole-sequence monotonicity, so no extra history-tracking beyond "compare this hop's match against the anchor it was searched from" is needed.

**Dialog-side gating (person-reported, this session):** for a hop chain whose directions are all the same (a single "before"/"after" hop, or 2+ hops that never mix directions), the monotonic-non-decreasing criterion above is trivial — a pure "before" chain always fails it (every match necessarily lands before its anchor, so the result is always empty) and a pure "after" chain always passes it (a no-op). The option only does something for a chain that mixes "before" and "after" hops. Rather than let a person tick the box and get a silently-empty result for the common single-hop "before" case, `#linkDialog` now gates the option itself: `updateLinkOrderEnforceAvailability()` hides `#linkOrderEnforceRow` outright (and unchecks `#linkOrderEnforceInput`, so toggling directions never leaves a stale checked-but-hidden state) whenever `linkHopRows`' current `.link-hop-dir` values aren't diverse (`dirs.length >= 2 && new Set(dirs).size > 1` is the showing condition). Called from `renderLinkHops()` on (re)build and from a `change` listener on every hop's direction `<select>`. (A first pass instead disabled the checkbox and showed an explanatory hint — replaced same session as too subtle to read as "off".) Both `linkExclusiveInput`/`linkOrderEnforceInput` are now the pill-shaped `.settings-switch` toggle used by the Settings dialog and the filter popup's Aa/NOT rows, not a plain checkbox, with Exclusive matches listed first and Enforce chronological order below it. The underlying `linkOrderEnforced` evaluation logic (`getEntriesFromBaked`/`getEntries`) is unchanged — this is purely a dialog affordance. See `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 190.

### Unmatched references (`_linkUnmatched`)

A reference that gets no pair — no key, no same-key candidate, no Nth match, or rejected by order enforcement — is dropped from the result (no placeholder pair entry), but `computeLinkPairs(cfg, refs, targets, fileId, unmatched)` collects it, in reference order, and the link branch of `evaluateFilterCondition` hands the list out through `meta.linkUnmatched`; `getEntriesUncached` stores it as **`node._linkUnmatched`**, runtime-only and recomputed with `_cache` exactly like `_gapMs` (no carrier serializes `_`-prefixed fields). A reference whose pair only the Δt condition dropped is not in it. For a chained link the entries are the outer step's references (pair entries; consumers flatten with `getTupleEntries`). Read by the dialog preview ("13 without end") and the Link view's "N without end" chip (`docs/ui-and-views.md`). Tested: GROUP link-unmatched.

### Correlation key: "Same …" (`linkKey`)

With several processes/threads logging, "the nearest following `position reached` after `move requested`" may belong to another axis/job/thread, and the pair's Δt is then silently wrong. `linkKey` restricts pairing to entries that belong together:

- **`{ column }`** — the same value in a column: Thread, Location, Method, a format's custom column, or **Source** (a merged file's `entry.sourceId`) — read by `entryGroupValue`, shared with the Gap filter's "measured per". An empty column value keys nothing.
- **`{ pattern }`** — the same capture(s) of a wildcard pattern (`axis [*:int]`, `job [*]`), matched against each entry's message with the extraction engine (`compileExtractPattern`/`wildcardMatch`; value conditions such as `[*:int>0]` apply). All captures joined form the key. An entry the pattern doesn't match keys nothing; a pattern without a capture is refused by the dialog.
