An entry without a key is never paired (a reference is dropped, a target is never a candidate). **Performance:** `computeLinkPairs` indexes the targets by key **once per recompute** (`Map` key → that key's targets, each list still ts-sorted), and each reference searches only its own key's list with the unchanged `findNthOccurrence(Excluding)`. So direction, N, the log-order tie-break, exclusivity (the running `usedIds` spans all keys) and order enforcement keep their exact meaning, just among same-key candidates. The key is read off the entry each hop **searches from** (`matchEntry` for a chained reference, see "Chained links"), so a multi-hop tuple stays within one thread/axis end to end. The dialog puts the key on every hop.

### Δt condition: "Only pairs with Δt > / < X" (`linkDt`)

`linkDt = { op: ">" | "<", ms }` keeps only tuples whose **span** is greater / less than `ms`. The span is `pair.dtMs = tsMax − tsMin` over the tuple's real entries: `buildPairEntry` stamps `tsMin`/`tsMax`/`dtMs`, carrying a nested pair's own `tsMin`/`tsMax` up, so a multi-hop tuple's `dtMs` is its **total span first → last** without walking it. It's a pure **post-filter on finished pairs**: `computeLinkPairs` tests it after the target has been claimed under "exclusive matches", so a pair the condition drops still consumes its end event and the pairing is identical with and without the condition (2026-10-04 fix: it used to run before the claim, freeing the end event for a later reference — with "Don't reuse" a Δt > 500 ms condition on the tour data produced 114 partly wrong pairs instead of 36 of 192). A reference whose pair the condition drops is not "without end". The multi-hop dialog sets it on the **last** hop only, whose pairs span the whole tuple; per-hop Δt conditions are deliberately not offered.

**Dialog** (`#linkDialog`, see "The link dialog" above): **Same** is a row of chips — first the suggestions of `suggestLinkKeys(startEntries, endEntries)`: every `name=` field present in the first match of both sides, as the key pattern `name=[*:word]` (`[*:word]` = the non-space value token), scored by distinct values per start entry; the best one with a score ≥ 0.9 (`LINK_KEY_SUGGEST_MIN_SCORE`, an ID such as `job`) is labelled "recommended · unique per start" (★ on phone) and **preselected**, otherwise "none" is. Then the column options (`groupColumnOptions`: Thread, Location, …, Source for a merged file), "none" and "pattern…" (reveals `#linkKeyPattern`). Why preselect: on the tour data "same Thread" pairs an aborted move with the next move's "Position reached" (453 s), only the job key gives the true answer (192 pairs, 13 without end, slowest 3.9 s). "Show only pairs with Δt [> / <] [value] [ms / s / min]" has a pill switch that greys its controls while off, off on every open. Below them, a **live preview** (150 ms debounce) renders the filter popup's result summary (`renderLiveResults` into `#linkResults`): "192 pairs · 13 without end · median 347ms · max 3.9s", with a Δt condition "36 of 192 pairs · …", the histogram, then samples **slowest first** and the first start without an end ("no end", warn-coloured); a hint warns when the longest pair exceeds 60 s (likely paired across different moves — try another Same key). It builds the would-be chain as one nested baked link (`buildLinkDialogChain` — the shape `createLinkNode`'s hop chaining produces) and evaluates it with `getEntriesFromBaked` over the shared root file, where Create places the node; the denominator is evaluated without the condition rather than filtered, since under exclusivity the two differ. The node name gets ` [same Thread]` / ` (Δt > 500ms)` appended (`linkOptionsNameSuffix`).

**Analyzing Δt**: an extraction on link pairs (a wildcard `text` filter under a link node) gets a synthetic **Δt (ms)** column next to Index / t (ms) — see `docs/extraction-and-plotting.md` → "Extraction table: synthetic Index + t(ms) columns". Plot t (ms) against Δt (ms) to see a duration drift over time.

**Persistence**: both are optional node fields (absent when unset), copied as fresh, sanitized objects (`sanitizeLinkDt`/`sanitizeLinkKey`, a malformed hand-edited value is dropped) by `copyLinkOptions` in every carrier — `bakeNodeCondition`, `materializeBakedAsNode` (Unpack), `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`, `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`. Both are editable through "Edit link…". Tested: **GROUP 290**, **link-dt-postfilter** (Δt), **GROUP 291** (key), **link-chain-edit** (suggestions, chain ⇄ steps, edit with undo), **link-dialog-v2** (dialog).

### Same-timestamp tie-break

**Person-reported follow-up** (screenshots of the multi-hop dialog + the Context/Filtered split): linking `"Target Real"` (anchor) to the nearest preceding `"Target Vir"` matched an entry roughly 11 seconds too early, even though the whole log clearly showed a `"Target Vir…"` line immediately followed by the `"Target Real…"` reference line. Root cause, confirmed before touching anything: `findNthOccurrence`'s `before`/`after` search compares timestamps with **strict** `<`/`>`. The log format only resolves to the millisecond, and this data bursts several log lines per control-loop tick at the *exact same* millisecond — so the `"Target Vir"` line sitting right next to the reference in the file shared its exact timestamp, made it a tie, and got excluded from "before" entirely (symmetrically true for "after" — both directions already treated ties as neither before nor after, this wasn't new or asymmetric, just surprising once a log has bursts). The search then kept walking backward past the whole tied cluster until it found an entry with a *strictly* earlier millisecond — 11 seconds earlier, from the previous cycle.

**Fix, exactly as requested**: when candidates tie with the reference on `.ts`, fall back to **log/array order** to decide before-vs-after, instead of excluding them.

- `buildOrderIndexMap(fileId)` builds a fresh `Map<entry.id, index>` from the root file's own `entries` array — "log order": parse order for an ordinary file, the already-chronologically-sorted union order for a merged file (see "The node tree"). Built once per `getEntries()` recompute of a `link` node (O(file size), same cost class as the `context` filter's own per-computation pass — not cached on the file node, to avoid new invalidation bookkeeping for what's still a rare, structural-change-triggered recompute; revisit if profiling ever shows this mattering on a file with many link nodes).
- `findNthOccurrence`/`findNthOccurrenceExcluding` now take the reference **entry** (not just its `ts`) plus this map: within the contiguous run of candidates sharing the reference's exact timestamp, the map locates where the reference itself would sit by log order, splitting that run into a "before" side and an "after" side — exactly mirroring what strict `ts` comparison already does for non-tied candidates, just scoped to the tie. If either id can't be resolved in the map (e.g. an unresolvable root file, or — see below — a chained link's synthetic outer reference), the comparison degrades gracefully back to "exclude the tie" rather than guessing.
- `buildPairEntry` had the same issue one level up: which side becomes `.first`/`.second` (display order, and the `⟶`-joined `message`/`raw`) used to default to "reference first" on any tie. It now takes the same `orderIndexMap` and, when both ids resolve, breaks the tie the same way — so the *displayed* pair order matches the log, not just the *matched* pair.
- `buildPairEntry` also gained `matchEntry` (the real `targetEntry` object a hop just matched, alongside the existing `matchTs`): a **chained** link's reference entry is a synthetic pair, whose own id never appears in a file's `entries` and so can't be looked up in the order map directly — `matchEntry` gives the *next* hop's tie-break a real entry id to resolve instead, the same way `matchTs` already gives it a real anchor timestamp (Bug 1 fix, see "Chained links" above). A plain, non-chained reference has neither field, so both simply fall back to the reference entry itself.

Verified against the exact reported shape (a decoy tie 11s earlier, then a same-millisecond burst with the target immediately preceding the reference, in both `before`/`after` directions), a plain no-ties case (regression guard — completely unaffected), and tie-break combined with exclusive matches (two references and two targets all sharing one timestamp, exclusivity still hands out the log-nearest *available* target to each). See `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 23.

**Same-timestamp entries keep log order everywhere a view re-sorts by time** (2026-09-28, person-reported). Every such sort is a stable `a.ts - b.ts`, so ties keep the order they were *collected* in, which is not always log order. Where a set is gathered out of log order, the sort goes through `chronoComparator(rank)` — `ts`, then `rank` (`buildOrderIndexMap` of the root file) on an exact tie; a NaN `ts` or an unranked id compares as before:
- **`"or"`** (`evaluateFilterCondition` → `combineBakedEntries`): A's matches, then B's, re-sorted.
- **Copy of a multi-selection** (`copyLogSelectionToClipboard`): `state.logMultiSelect` is in click order.
- **Temp anchor position** (`tempAnchorInsertIndex`): lands inside its tied cluster at its log position instead of after the whole cluster.

The meta-format merge is handled at the source instead — see `docs/persistence-and-sync.md` → `fillMergedEntries`' `logOrder`. Tests: GROUP 314.

### Backward compatibility

A serialized `link` node with no `linkOrderEnforced`/`linkExclusive` fields at all (e.g. hand-edited) still materializes cleanly with both flags defaulting `false` — verified by a regression test. A multi-hop tuple built through the dialog does **not** get its own `filterType`; it's a plain `link` node whose `bakedA` nests a previous hop's own baked condition (see "Chained links" above), so it round-trips through save/load exactly the way manually-chained links already did — `bakedA`/`bakedB` are plain data, copied wholesale by every persistence carrier with no ref-resolution step at all (see "Export/library" below).

### Minimap integration

The Link view's own pair-brace ("Klammer") selection also marks its pair's real entries on the timeline minimap, which is now shown during the Link view for this reason — see "Timeline minimap" below for the full mechanism.

### Interaction model: block selection vs. single-line jump

The Link view distinguishes two selection units, both tracked by `linkSelectedPairIndex` (an index into `linkPairsData`, not a DOM class — see that variable's own comment, since a virtualized `.pair-block` can be torn down and rebuilt between clicks):

- **Whole block/pair** — a **single click anywhere in a `.pair-block`** (the brace *or* any of its rows) selects that pair as a whole, toggling off if the same block is clicked again. **Up/Down arrow keys** (`moveLinkSelection(delta)`) move this same block selection one pair at a time, clamped at both ends, scrolling the target block into view via `linkBlockOffsets` and re-rendering the virtualized window (`renderLinkVisibleBlocks`) if the move stepped outside it. **Alt+Enter**, when a block is selected, opens the same "Filter for this ___" dialog **right-click brace → "Filter for this message" already does**: both pass the *pair* object (not a single real entry) into `openFilterForEntryColumn`, which reads the pair's already-combined `message` (`PAIR_SEPARATOR`-joined, see above) — so the resulting wildcard pattern always spans the **whole tuple**, matching what the brace's own context-menu item produces byte-for-byte.
- **Single line** — **double-click on a row** (`buildPairRow`'s own `dblclick`) is unaffected by any of the above: it always jumps to that one real entry via `revealInHighlightView`, independent of whatever block is currently selected (and that jump's own `applySelection()` call in turn *clears* `linkSelectedPairIndex`, since a real single-entry selection supersedes a stale block one — same mechanism `minimapMarkedEntries()` relies on). Right-click on a row (vs. the brace) still opens the context menu scoped to just that row's own column/entry, not the whole pair — a separate, narrower path from "Filter for this message" on the brace.

Person-reported gap this closes (this session): previously a row click did nothing, Up/Down was a no-op in the Link view, and keyboard Alt+Enter picked up whichever single entry `state.selectedId` last held from a prior row double-click (since a pair's synthetic id is never registered in `entryIndex`) — wildcarding only one side of the tuple instead of the whole pair. See `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 168.

**Same gap, found again in the viewBar toolbar (a later session):** the toolbar's own "Message"/"Extract" row-action buttons (`singleMessageActionEntry`, behind `handleRowActionClick`'s `filterForMessage`/`extractMessage` cases) were never taught the pair check above — they resolved their target purely via `state.selectedId` (`currentRowActionEntry()`), so selecting a pair block and clicking "Extract" wildcarded whichever single real entry a *prior* row double-click had left in `state.selectedId`, not the selected pair. `singleMessageActionEntry()` now runs the identical check Alt+Enter uses (Link view on screen, `state.entriesView === "filter"`, a pair selected via `linkSelectedPairIndex`) and returns `linkPairsData[linkSelectedPairIndex].pair` before ever falling back to `currentRowActionEntry()`. See `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 213.

### Testing note (deviation from the requirements doc's suggested test layout)

`REQUIREMENTS-link-chaining-and-multiway.md` shipped with a standalone companion, `tests/link-chaining.spec.js`, meant to be copied into the project's `tests/` folder and run on its own. Its BASELINE/TARGET assertions (originally written "informational, pre-implementation" — always exiting 0) were instead folded into `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` as **Group 22**, now as real pass/fail assertions, alongside new coverage for the two opt-in options, the multi-hop dialog, and persistence — no separate spec file was added. This follows the project's own established testing convention (see `tests/README.md`, "Extending this suite": one consolidated suite, extended every session, not a new throwaway file per feature) rather than the requirements doc's suggested layout; noted here per that doc's own "if a different shape is chosen... note the deviation in PROJECT.md" allowance.

## Self-contained AND/OR/LINK: `baked` / `bakedA`/`bakedB`, placement, and Unpack

`and`/`or` nodes carry `node.baked` — an **array of 2 or more baked conditions** (one per selected filter, in selection order; `createAndOrNode(ids, mode)`, `mode` "and"/"or"). `link` nodes carry `node.bakedA`/`node.bakedB` (reference + target). Each baked condition is a **flat, self-contained copy of one side's own single condition** (`filterType`, `value`, and whichever of `caseSensitive`/`columns`/`isRegex`/`contextBefore`/`contextAfter`/`countBefore`/`countAfter`/`linkDirection`/`linkN`/`linkOrderEnforced`/`linkExclusive`/`linkDt`/`linkKey`/`bakedA`/`bakedB` apply for that `filterType` — see `bakeNodeCondition`) — **never** a node-id reference, never an ancestor chain. Baked once at creation time (or Unpack, below); after that, `bakedA`/`bakedB` never look at `state.nodes[...]` again. Deleting, renaming, moving, or replacing the original source node(s) has **zero effect** on the combiner's result — which is the whole reason the two sides are baked rather than referenced by id.

**What can be a side.** `canBeCombined` rejects two kinds of node for `and`/`or`:
- a **`link`** node, whose result is synthetic pair entries (`buildPairEntry`) with ids that never appear in a plain entry pool — an AND over one would always be empty, an OR type-mixed. The bulk menu therefore offers only "Link…" when either selected node is a link; chaining onto a link is what `createLinkNode` is for, and its evaluator does understand pair entries.
- a **combiner with no baked sides**, which is what a filter file or library preset written before this model materializes as (its old node-id references are meaningless here). Such a node evaluates to nothing, is refused by Combine and by Unpack, and is rejected outright by `importFilterJson`'s validation rather than landing as a filter that silently matches nothing.

`getEntries()`'s `and`/`or`/`link` branch is no longer a special case at all: it reads its own input entries the ORDINARY way every other filter type does — `getEntries(node.parentId)` — then evaluates the baked conditions as predicates over that pool via `getEntriesFromBaked(baked, poolEntries, fileId)`, a one-line wrapper around `evaluateFilterCondition(cond, parentEntries, fileId, meta)` — **the one evaluator of a filter condition**: `getEntriesUncached` calls it with the node itself (a node and a baked snapshot carry the same field names), so every per-filterType branch (`textFilterMatches`/`wildcardMatch`/`compileRegexFilter`/`compileExtractPattern`/time-range checks/`findNthOccurrence(Excluding)`/`buildPairEntry`, the inversion rule) exists once and a baked side is identical to a real standalone filter of that type by construction. The node-only side data (`_gapMs`, `_contextRanges`, `_anchorIds`) comes back through the `meta` object only `getEntriesUncached` passes; a baked side passes none and never builds it. The evaluator recurses into `baked.baked` (nested combiner) / `baked.bakedA`/`baked.bakedB` (nested **baked link**, a link-of-link chain — see "Chained links" below). `and` = ALL N predicates true, `or` = ANY true (`combineBakedEntries`, chronologically sorted for `or`), applied per-entry over `getEntries(node.parentId)`; `link` builds its reference-side/target-side entry sets the same way (`getEntriesFromBaked(bakedA, ...)` / `getEntriesFromBaked(bakedB, ...)`) and runs the existing nearest-occurrence pairing machinery over those two sets exactly as before. `node.parentId` is what determines this node's INPUT pool (exactly like a plain `"text"` filter) — moving the node just re-chains it onto a different parent's output; `bakedA`/`bakedB` are never touched by a move.

**Critical correctness property, explicitly required and tested**: baking captures ONLY the clicked node's own single condition, never anything from its ancestors. If filter A sits nested under some unrelated filter C ("only entries after 10:00"), combining A with B into an AND matches "A's own condition AND B's own condition" against whatever the AND node's OWN parentId chain provides — C's restriction never implicitly leaks in.

No cycle guard is needed any more: `bakedA`/`bakedB` hold plain data, not node-id references, so there is nothing to cycle through except normal recursion into a nested baked link, bounded by ordinary data-structure depth.

**Name and tooltip.** An AND/OR node is named by joining every source's display name with " ∧ " / " ∨ "; the tree row truncates with an ellipsis and carries the full name as its `title` tooltip.

**Placement on creation.** `createAndOrNode`/`createLinkNode` always insert the new node as a fresh top-level child of the first input's root file (`root.children.unshift(...)`, same "independent, near the top" placement `syncBookmarksFilterNode`/`createSelectionFilterNode` already use) — regardless of where the two inputs themselves sit in the tree. From there, the node can be moved anywhere by the user like any other node: moving it is pure display repositioning, changing only `parentId` (and therefore its input pool), never `bakedA`/`bakedB`.

**Unpack** (tree context menu, any `and`/`or`/`link` node, next to Rename/Delete): **purely additive, no fresh combiner**. `unpackAndOrLinkNode` materializes `node.baked` (N conditions) or `node.bakedA`/`node.bakedB` (link) into real, visible, brand-new sibling filter nodes (`materializeBakedAsNode`, same `filterType`/fields), inserted right after the original node's own position. The original node itself is left **completely untouched** — same id, same `bakedA`/`bakedB`, same result — since its own condition already works fine once its two inputs are visible again; there is nothing to replace, so no new combiner node is created and nothing is deleted. Unpack's only purpose is to make the two building blocks visible and editable again, since an `and`/`or` combiner has no dedicated edit UI (see `FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #58; a `link` node has "Edit link…", see "The link dialog"). The menu entry is offered only for a node that actually carries both baked sides.

**Persistence**: `baked` / `bakedA`/`bakedB` are rows of `FILTER_NODE_FIELDS` (see PROJECT.md's "Known gotchas") and so reach all the persistence carriers as a plain, generic value copy — no id-remapping logic anywhere, since there's no id inside them: `cloneSubtree` (deep-copies `bakedA`/`bakedB` like any other field), `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree` (undo/redo), `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson` (see "Export/library: just this filter vs. with ancestor chain" below), and `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters` (session cache).

Regression-tested: **Group 128** — the exact user repro (combine "Some" AND "Entry", delete "Some", verify unchanged, delete "Entry", verify still unchanged), ancestor-independence (a filter nested under an unrelated ancestor C combines using only its own condition), placement under FILE on creation for both AND/OR and LINK, Unpack (original node left completely untouched, no fresh combiner created, result unchanged, two new visible siblings materialized), and all four persistence carriers round-tripping `bakedA`/`bakedB` as plain data. **Group 7** — copy/cut/paste and drag-and-drop (same-file and cross-file, both now a plain reparent/clone with no special-casing).

## Export/library: "just this filter" vs. "with ancestor chain"

**Generalized this session** — this is no longer an `and`/`or`/`link`-specific concern. The previous `and`/`or`/`link`-specific "Include source filters used by combined nodes?" dialog (`openIncludeInputsPrompt`) is removed outright (it was also the cause of a reported bug: it could appear unconditionally at app startup instead of only during an actual save/export action). Every single-filter Save JSON/Save-to-library action now asks a general **"Just this filter" vs. "Include ancestor chain"** question (`openExportScopePrompt`, a small modal in the `#linkDialog`/`#contextDialog` style, `#exportScopeDialog`) — for ANY filter type, not just combiners:

- **"Just this filter"** — `serializeFilterBranch(nodeId, false)`: exports exactly the one clicked node, no ancestors, no subtree. For `and`/`or`/`link` this trivially includes its own `bakedA`/`bakedB`, which are already fully self-contained; for any other filter type, it's just that one node.
- **"Include ancestor chain"** — `serializeFilterBranch(nodeId, true)`: today's original chain+subtree export (the ancestor chain down to the clicked node, plus its full subtree) — unchanged in shape, just no longer combiner-specific.

**Import/apply placement (both cases)**: the imported branch — whether the single node or the full chain — attaches as a child of **whatever node is currently active/selected at the moment of import**, never hardcoded to FILE (every exported root is tagged `attach:"target"`; `materializeSerializedRoots`/`importFilterJson` resolve it to the import target's own id). "Just this filter" attaches exactly one node there; "include ancestor chain" attaches the whole chain there, its own internal relative structure unchanged — only its root's attachment point moves.

This same `includeAncestors` parameter is shared by Save/Load filter JSON (`saveFilterToFile`/`importFilterJson`) and the reusable filter library (`saveFilterToLibrary`/`applyFilterFromLibrary`, which hands off to `importFilterJson` unchanged) — see `docs/persistence-and-sync.md` for the storage-layer detail.

Regression-tested: **Group 11** — both scopes round-trip correctly onto a fresh file at a non-FILE target, for an `and`/`or`/`link` node (`bakedA`/`bakedB` traveling as plain data). **Group 135** — the general option for an ORDINARY filter type too, import placement at a non-FILE target for both a plain filter and a combiner, the prompt appearing as part of the actual save action (not just save-to-library), and a regression guard that no dialog shows unconditionally at startup.

## Time filters: unified `"timerange"` type, one node per window, draft window, edit dialog

One filterType, `"timerange"`, covers all from/to time filtering — `value: { from, to }`, either bound `null` meaning unbounded on that side. `getEntries`'s branch is a plain `(from == null || e.ts >= from) && (to == null || e.ts <= to)` filter over `parentEntries`. **Every creation path goes through one helper, `applyTimeWindow(targetId, from, to)`**: the minimap draft's **Filter** button (`createTimeRangeFilterFromDrag`), the row context menu's and row actions' "Filter after/before this row" (one bound set, the other `null`), "Time filter from selection" (both bounds, next paragraph), and the time-range dialog in create mode. Only the folder minimap's "Merge (window)" still calls `createFilterNode` directly (it attaches the window to a brand-new merge node).

**One node per window** (usability round C): `applyTimeWindow` never nests a second time node where one would do.
- Target is a time node (`"timerange"`, or a legacy `"after"`/`"before"` one — its bounds come from `timeRangeOfNode`, and the update converts it to `"timerange"`; undo restores the legacy node): it is updated **in place** (`updateTimeRangeFilterNodeWithUndo`, so undoable) and stays active. A non-null new bound overwrites; a `null` new bound (one-bound action) keeps the node's existing bound, so "Filter after" then "Filter before" ends in one node with both bounds. If the merge would invert the window (`from > to`), only the new bound is kept and the other side opens. Two given bounds that arrive reversed are swapped.
- Anything else: a new `"timerange"` child via `createFilterNode`.

**Labels** (`timeRangeFilterName(value, nodeId)`, stored in `node.name` at create/update; `timeRangeBoundLabel` formats one bound): `08:38:24 – 08:39:52 · 1m 28s` (en dash, then `formatMs` of the span); open bounds read `from 08:38:24` / `until 08:45:48`; no bound at all `any time`. A bound's date is left out when it lies on the same local day as the root file's first entry, otherwise `MM-DD ` is prefixed (`01-16 00:03:10`); milliseconds (`.mmm`) appear only when both bounds are set and the span is under 10 s. Files without a date in their `tsFormat` (1970) show the bare time; plain-text files keep line bounds in the same shape (`line 5 – line 90`, `from line 5`, no duration). The tree row's tooltip (`timeRangeFullTitle`) shows the full bounds with date and milliseconds. Why: the old `≥ 08:38:24.113 → …` names were indistinguishable once truncated in the tree. In the tree the generated label wraps onto at most 2 lines (`-webkit-line-clamp`), breaking only after the " – " / " · " separators: `renderNode` renders it as nowrap `.tl-seg` spans in a `.tree-label-wrap` (textContent unchanged; custom labels and all other nodes stay single-line). A timerange label with a duration renders the bounds in a shrinking `.tl-range` (2-line clamp, ellipsis) and the duration after the last " · " in a `flex:none` `.tl-dur`, so a narrow tree cuts the bounds, never the duration.

**"Time filter from selection"** (person-requested): right-clicking a 2+ row multi-selection (`state.logMultiSelect`) offers `#ctxTimeRangeFromSelection` alongside "Filter after/before this row" — hidden for a single selected/right-clicked row, same 2+ threshold `currentSelectionRowIds` uses for "Add to selection". Both bounds are set at once, to the earliest and latest `ts` among the selected rows' entries (looked up via `entryIndex`), so the created filter covers every entry between them — not just the ones that happened to be selected.

**Legacy `"after"`/`"before"` types**: the single-bound predecessors of `"timerange"` (value was a plain `number`, not `{from,to}`). Both stay in `FILTER_TYPES` and `getEntries` keeps their branches (`ts >= value` / `ts <= value`) — purely so a session/export saved before this feature keeps reading correctly. **Nothing creates them anymore.** Editing one through the dialog (F2 or tree right-click "Edit filter…", both gated on `isTimeFilterType(filterType)`) migrates it to `"timerange"` in place — one-way, via `updateTimeRangeFilterNode`; there's no UI to go back to the single-bound shape, which is fine since the two are behaviorally identical whenever only one bound is set. `timeRangeOfNode(node)` normalizes any of the three shapes into a plain `{from,to}` pair, which is what lets the dialog's edit mode work uniformly across all three.

**Why one node, not after+before+AND**: the drag-select feature originally built a range from two separate filters (`"after"` + `"before"`) combined by an `"and"` node — reusing the existing AND-combinator machinery meant zero new filter-type code, but produced three tree nodes for one conceptual filter. Person-reported follow-up asked for a single filter instead; `"timerange"` replaced the after+before+AND shape everywhere it was used. Because the new `{from,to}` value is still carried under each filter node's **existing** generic `value` field (not a new top-level field like `link`'s `linkDirection`/`linkN` or `context`'s `contextBefore`/`contextAfter`), **no persistence-carrier code needed touching** beyond adding `"timerange"` to `FILTER_TYPES` — `cloneSubtree`/`snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`/`serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`/`serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters` all already copy/serialize `value` generically for every filter type (see CLAUDE.md's "Known gotchas" note — this is the case where that gotcha turned out not to apply, verified by round-tripping a `"timerange"` node through the real Save/Load filter JSON path in `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 32). This is where `value`'s **immutability by convention** matters: `cloneSubtree`/`snapshotSubtree`/`captureNodeFields` copy `value` by reference — fine for the primitive-number shapes, aliasing for the object/array ones (`timerange`, `idset`, `level`) — so every write must replace `node.value` wholesale (`node.value = { from, to }`) rather than mutating the existing object in place. `"timerange"` follows this from the start; `addRowsToSelectionFilter` (the `idset` selection-filter grower) originally did not, and pushing into the shared array made a copy/pasted duplicate of the node grow along with the original and retroactively rewrote the undo stack's "before" capture. It now rebuilds the array (`node.value = node.value.concat(added)`).

**Bugfix, 2026-08-28, person-reported ("no longer works")**: the minimap drag's anchor (`minimapDragStartTs`, formerly `minimapDragStartX`) is captured as a real **timestamp** at mousedown, not a raw `minimapWidth`-unit x position. A mid-drag `renderTimelineMinimap()` rebuild — the same class of event the overlay's own out-of-`<svg>` placement above already has to survive — can change `minimapTMin`/`minimapTMax` (a tail tick extends them) or `minimapWidth` (a resize) out from under an in-progress gesture; re-evaluating a stored pixel-unit x against the *new* time range at mouseup no longer pointed at the entry actually dragged from, and in the worst case could flip the from/to order and silently fail the `toTs > fromTs` guard — no filter created, no error, the drag just appearing not to work. A timestamp anchor is immune: every pixel position the gesture needs (overlay, threshold check, final range) is re-derived from it via `minimapTsToX`/`minimapXToTs` against whatever is currently live. Regression-tested in Group 31 with a tail tick landing mid-drag.

**Drag → draft window, then Filter** (`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` item, reworked in usability round C): click-drag across the minimap's bars no longer creates a filter on release; it leaves a **draft window** (`minimapDraft`, `{from, to}` timestamps — see "Timeline minimap" below) that the person can adjust and then turn into something. A pixel-distance threshold (`MINIMAP_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX = 3`, `MINIMAP_TOUCH_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX = 8` for touch) tells a real drag apart from a plain click (which still falls through to click-to-jump and discards the draft); a one-shot `minimapDragSuppressClick` flag stops the browser's trailing `click` after the mouseup from being misread as a jump. The live overlay while dragging (`#timelineMinimapDragRect`/`#timelineMinimapDragLabel`) and the draft's pieces are plain `<div>`s positioned *outside* the minimap's `<svg>`, so `renderTimelineMinimap()`'s full `innerHTML` rebuild (tail tick, level toggle) never wipes them, and they stay independent of the range-indicator rectangles. Right-click / long-press on the minimap still opens the dialog in create mode, prefilled with the clicked point as **both** bounds.

**Time-range dialog** (`#timeRangeDialog`, `openTimeRangeDialog(mode, targetId, prefill)`/`closeTimeRangeDialog()`): `mode: "create"` attaches a window under `targetId` through `applyTimeWindow`; `mode: "edit"` updates the node at `targetId` in place (migrating a legacy node, see above) — the same targetId-means-different-things-per-mode convention `openFilterPopup`/`openEditFilterPopup` use. Fields:
- **Time-only text fields** (`HH:MM:SS.mmm`, `inputmode="decimal"`, monospace; `parseTimeOfDay` accepts `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS`, `HH:MM:SS.m{1,3}`, also a comma before the fraction); invalid text shows an inline error and does not submit. The date is entered **once**: when the root file and both prefilled bounds lie on one local day, a read-only chip (`Thu 2026-01-15`) implies it; otherwise each bound gets its own `<input type="date">` (prefilled from the bound, or the file's first/last day when empty). Times are local, matching `formatTime`/`parseTimestamp`.
- **−1s / +1s buttons** on both sides of each field (also ArrowUp/ArrowDown, Shift = 1 min); on an empty field they start from the file's first (From) / last (To) entry.
- **Empty field = unbounded** — no separate "infinity" checkbox, same convention as the value-assertion dialog's min/max fields. Both empty is rejected; a reversed From/To is silently swapped.
- **Live meta line** (`updateTimeRangeDialogMeta`): `Duration 1m 28s · 104 entries` (just `104 entries` when a bound is open). The count is over the node the window applies to: the target's result in create mode, the edited node's parent result in edit mode.
- **Plain-text files**: whole-number "line" fields, no date or chip, ±1 means one line (Shift ±10), no duration.
- Touch: no autofocus (`isCoarsePointer`, the keyboard would pop up); ±1s buttons are at least 44×34 px.

## Timeline minimap: bars, zoom, draft window, range indicators, selection markers

A density strip above the log table (`renderTimelineMinimap(rootId, viewEntries)`, called from `renderTable()` and `renderLinkView()` — see below). Grey background bars show entry density across the **whole root file** (memoized, `minimapBgCache` — see "Known limitations" resolved entry); colored overlay bars show `viewEntries` on top, one bar per bucket colored by the worst (most severe) level present. `minimapInteractive = !state.sortColumn` withholds only the features that assume "adjacent row = adjacent moment" (click-to-jump, drag-select, wheel zoom, the two range rectangles) during a column sort; hover tooltip and the selection marker(s) stay available regardless, since neither depends on row adjacency.

**View window and zoom** (usability round C; section comment "Minimap zoom" above `minimapTsToX`): the strip shows the whole root file or one time window of it. `minimapTMin`/`minimapTMax` are always the bounds of what is **drawn** (the file's own span is `minimapFileTMin`/`TMax`), so `minimapTsToX`/`XToTs`/`BucketOf` and everything built on them — range rects, selection markers, hover tooltip, click-to-jump, drag, long-press — work unchanged inside a zoomed view; in `"entries"` binning the drawn range is the index slice `[minimapIdxLo, minimapIdxLo + minimapIdxN)` of the root entries inside the window. `minimapBgCache` is keyed on the view too, and the slice is found with `lowerBoundByTs`, so zooming stays cheap on the tail-tick hot path.
- **State**: `minimapViewTrail`, the breadcrumb stack (`{from, to}` per crumb, the last is the current view, empty = whole file). It resets when the minimap's root file changes and is **not persisted**. Hooks: `setMinimapView(from, to)` (push a crumb), `minimapViewReset()`, `minimapViewGoTo(depth)`, `minimapViewZoomAt(ts, factor)`. Minimum view span 2 s (`MINIMAP_MIN_SPAN_MS`; 2 lines for plain-text files).
- **Breadcrumbs** in `#timelineMinimapMeta`, before Start/End while zoomed: `Whole file › 08:37:05–08:40:27 › …`, each crumb a button (`minimapCrumbsHtml`), the last one disabled, followed by a resolution hint (`minimapResolutionText`: `174 ms/px`, `2.41 s/px`, `entries/px` or `lines/px`).
- **Wheel** over the minimap (desktop) zooms around the cursor (factor 0.8 in / 1.25 out, non-passive listener so the page never scrolls meanwhile); consecutive wheel notches **replace** the top crumb (`minimapViewWheelTop`) instead of piling one crumb per notch; zooming out past the whole file resets the view.
- **Pinch** (touch): two fingers on the strip zoom around their midpoint with the same logic (`minimapViewZoomAt`, anchor via `minimapAnchorTsAtClientX`, top crumb replaced, reset past the whole file, 2 s floor). A capture-phase `pointerdown` on `window` tracks the touch pointers; the second finger cancels a running draft or handle drag (the previous draft comes back, as on `pointercancel`), and lifting the fingers starts nothing — no draft, jump or long-press (`minimapPinchTail` swallows the trailing click). `touch-action: pan-y` already keeps the browser from page-zooming.
- **Phone** (`body.layout-phone`): the strip is 36 px tall (was 14); the meta line stays hidden at rest, and a 24 px crumb line (`.has-crumbs`, strip 60 px in total) shows while zoomed or while a draft exists — there it also carries the draft text in seconds instead of the floating label.

**Draft window** (`minimapDraft`, `{from, to}` as **timestamps**, so it survives every re-render, zoom and resize; discarded on a root-file change and after Filter/Edit…): a drag (mouse or touch, same thresholds and timestamp anchor as before) ends in a draft instead of a filter. `renderMinimapDraft()` repositions its parts, all outside the `<svg>`: the `.selected` overlay (the drag rect), a floating label `08:37:22.267 – 08:40:10.437 · 2m 48s · 516 entries` (`minimapDraftLabelText`; the count is over `minimapLastViewEntries`, i.e. the active node's result), **two handles** (22 px hit area, `ew-resize`) that each move one bound and swap when they cross, and an **action bar** below the strip: **Label and action bar** (desktop/tablet) form one group inside the strip, `[label] 6px [Zoom | Filter | Edit… | ×]`, placed by the pure `minimapDraftGroupLeft({W, xa, xb, fromVisible, toVisible, groupW})`: centered on the window when it fits between the visible handles with 14px clearance, else beside the window on the roomier side (right of the to-handle / left of the from-handle), always clamped to [4, W-4]; a hidden handle is not in the way, and the label/bar are drawn above the handles (z-index) so text is never cut by one. Nothing of the draft UI extends below the strip; on the phone the label stays hidden and the bar sits below the strip as before.
- **Zoom** — view = draft ±10 %, pushes a crumb; the draft stays.
- **Filter** — `applyTimeWindow` on the active node (so it updates a time node in place — see "Time filters"); the button reads **Update filter** when the active node is a time node (`isTimeFilterType`: `"timerange"` or legacy `"after"`/`"before"`). Discards the draft.
- **Edit…** — opens the time-range dialog in create mode on the active node, prefilled with the draft.
- **×** or **Esc** — discard. A plain click on the strip (no drag) discards the draft and does click-to-jump as before.

**Adopted window** (`minimapAdoptedWindow()`, derived from the active node on every render, never stored): while the active node is a time filter (`"timerange"`, or legacy `"after"`/`"before"` via `timeRangeOfNode`) of the displayed root, its window is shown like a draft — overlay, label, handles — but **without** the action bar; an open bound sits at the file edge and has no handle. Moving a handle turns it into a normal draft (`{from, to, adoptedFrom}`) with the bar and **Update filter**; × / Esc drop only that draft, so the node's own window shows again; switching the active node drops a moved draft and the adopted window follows the new node. A new drag elsewhere replaces it with a fresh draft; a plain click still jumps.

**Binning mode** (`minimapBinningMode`, **Settings → Timeline minimap → "Minimap binning"**, `"time"` | `"entries"`, default `"time"`, `philogg-minimap-binning-mode`, FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #2, person-approved design): controls what a bar's horizontal position is proportional to.
- **`"time"`** (default, the original/only behavior before this session): a bar's x is proportional to where its `entry.ts` sits in `[minimapTMin, minimapTMax]`, the root file's full time span.
- **`"entries"`**: a bar's x is proportional to the entry's **ordinal position** among the root file's own entries (`0..entryCount-1`) instead — a burst of fast activity spreads out evenly across the width instead of compressing into a few pixels, and a long idle stretch stops eating most of the width just because it covers a lot of wall-clock time.

The mode is deliberately **visualization-only** and lives entirely behind a shared conversion layer, three functions:
- **`minimapTsToX(ts)`**: in `"entries"` mode, binary-searches `minimapRootEntries` (`lowerBoundByTs`, the same helper used everywhere else in the file for a chronological array — root file entries are guaranteed chronological, see "The node tree" above) for the entry's index, clamps it to `[0, len-1]`, and returns `idx / (len - 1) * minimapWidth`; in `"time"` mode it's the original `(ts - minimapTMin) / (minimapTMax - minimapTMin) * minimapWidth`.
- **`minimapXToTs(x)`**: the inverse. In `"entries"` mode, converts x to an index (`Math.round(x / minimapWidth * (len - 1))`, clamped) and returns `minimapRootEntries[idx].ts` — the **real timestamp of the actual entry** that pixel resolves to, not an interpolated point in time. This is the whole reason nothing above this conversion layer needed to change: every caller that used to get an approximate time (click-to-jump's `lowerBoundByTs` lookup, the draft window's bounds, the right-click dialog's prefill) now just gets a more exact one, and already handles "some entry's real ts" correctly.
- **`minimapBucketOf(ts)`**: resolves a timestamp to its density-bucket index, mirroring the same branch — index-proportional bucketing (`Math.floor(idx / len * bucketCount)`, clamped) in `"entries"` mode, the pre-existing time-proportional formula in `"time"` mode. `minimapBarSpan(ts)` (below) and the hover tooltip both call this instead of re-deriving either formula by hand, so neither can ever disagree with the render pass (see that function's own comment) about which bucket a ts belongs to.

`minimapRootEntries` (the active node's root file entries, set in `renderTimelineMinimap` right alongside `minimapTMin`/`minimapTMax`) backs the `"entries"` branch of all three. `renderTimelineMinimap`'s own `bgCounts`/`ovCounts` passes bucket by array position/`buildOrderIndexMap` lookup directly instead of calling `minimapBucketOf` per entry (an O(file size) render pass calling a binary search per entry would cost O(file size · log file size) instead of O(file size)) — but use the exact same formula, so the render pass and the interaction layer can never disagree either.

**Expected side-effect of `"entries"` mode, not a bug**: the grey background bars render essentially flat/uniform — every bucket covers the same fixed slice of the file's line count by construction, so background density stops varying bucket-to-bucket once binning is by index instead of by time. The value in this mode is entirely in the overlay bars, which still show where in the file's line order the current filtered/leveled result concentrates.

Persistence: `minimapBinningMode` is a plain `localStorage` UI preference (`initMinimapBinningModeSetting`), same tier as `hideMinimapFullRangeInFullView`/`contextExpandStep` below — **not** a filter-node field, so it needs no persistence-carrier threading (`cloneSubtree`/`snapshotSubtree`/`serializeFilterBranch`/session-cache — see CLAUDE.md's "Known gotchas"). The Settings `<select>`'s `change` listener re-renders the minimap immediately (`renderTimelineMinimap(minimapLastRootId, minimapLastViewEntries)` + `updateMinimapRenderedRange()`, the same targeted re-render the window-resize handler already uses) rather than a full `render()`, since flipping the toggle doesn't change the active filter/view, only how the same `viewEntries` get laid out across the width.

**`minimapBarSpan(ts)`**: maps a timestamp to the full pixel `{left, right}` span of the density bar it falls into (via `minimapBucketOf`, mode-aware — see above), as opposed to `minimapTsToX(ts)`'s single continuous point for that moment. Anything that needs to align with the bars *as drawn* (the two range rectangles below) uses this instead of `minimapTsToX` directly — using the raw point used to leave a rectangle's edge sitting short of the bar it was meant to fully cover (person-reported bug, fixed in an earlier session — see `tests/philogg.regression.test.js` Group 33).

**Two range-indicator rectangles**, both bucket-aligned via `minimapBarSpan`:
- `#minimapFullRangeRect` (`updateMinimapFullRange`) — the whole time span `minimapLastViewEntries` (the last `viewEntries` passed to `renderTimelineMinimap`) covers, i.e. everything the active filter/Link node currently matches, independent of scroll or virtualization. Scans for real min/max rather than assuming the first/last array elements are the extremes — true for the table view's chronological `currentViewEntries`, **not** guaranteed for the Link view's flattened pair entries (a "before" hop's match can land earlier than its own reference — see "Link filter" above), so the one function stays correct for both callers. **Settings → Behavior → "Hide minimap's covered-timespan box in Context view"** (FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #8, `hideMinimapFullRangeInFullView`/`philogg-hide-minimap-full-range-in-full-view`, default **off**): when on, this box hides itself whenever the Context tab is the one on screen (`fhLayout === "tabs" && fhActiveTab === "highlight"`). It dates from when that view always covered the whole log, which made the box meaningless there; since the Context view rework it shows the active node's own result and the box is informative again, so this is kept purely as an opt-out for a quieter minimap rather than as a fix. Left alone in Stacked layout (the Filtered pane is visible alongside the Context pane there) and, of course, whenever the Filtered tab is what's showing.
- `#minimapRenderedRangeRect` (`updateMinimapRenderedRange`) — nested inside the full range, covering only the entries that currently have DOM rows in whichever pane is **actually on screen right now**. Branches on the same `fhLayout`/`fhActiveTab` check as the toggle above: Context tab active → `highlightBody.scrollTop`/`clientHeight` over `currentHighlightViewEntries` (not gated on `minimapInteractive` — no column sort exists in the Context view); otherwise → `tableBody.scrollTop`/`clientHeight` over `currentViewEntries`, as before, still withheld during a column sort. Both branches share `minimapRenderedSpan(entries, scrollEl, rowOffsets)` for the actual index/pixel math — keyed on the offsets array's own presence rather than on `needsRowOffsets()`, since the Context view always has one (its gap strips make row tops variable regardless of the multiline/notes toggles) (indices clamped to the list's bounds on both ends — an earlier version only clamped the lower bound, so switching to a much smaller filtered result while scrolled deep into a larger one indexed past the array's end and threw). A guard at the very top hides the rect unconditionally whenever the Link view is on screen (`linkWrap.style.display !== "none"`) — the Link view has no row virtualization at all (every pair-block is a real DOM node already), so there's no meaningful "rendered subset" there regardless of which fh tab was last active; this can't rely on simply never being called during the Link view any more, since `renderHighlightView()` (below) keeps refreshing the Context view's own data in the background even then. `renderTable()`/`renderHighlightView()` each call this themselves right after they run, the `#tableBody`/`#highlightBody` scroll listeners call it rAF-batched on scroll, the window-resize and sidebar-resize drag handlers call it unconditionally whenever the minimap itself is visible (previously gated on the table view specifically — that gate would have wrongly skipped it while the Context tab was on screen), and `showFhTab`/`applyFhView` call both range functions on every tab/layout switch so flipping panes re-evaluates them immediately, without waiting on an unrelated scroll or render.

**Selection marker(s)** (`updateMinimapSelectionMarkers`, into `<g id="minimapSelectionMarkers">`): a thin vertical line + small flag at the exact `minimapTsToX(ts)` position of each currently "marked" entry. `minimapMarkedEntries()` resolves what's marked, in priority order: (1) a Link view pair currently selected via its brace (`.pair-brace`, "Klammer" — see "Link filter" above) — every real entry the pair/tuple is made of, read off a `data-entry-ids` attribute `renderLinkView` stashes on the brace at render time, gated on the Link view actually being the *current* active view (a stale `.pair-selected` left over from navigating away must not keep marking its old entries — `renderLinkView` only clears it by rebuilding `#linkBody` from scratch the next time *it* runs, which doesn't happen just from switching away); (2) otherwise the ordinary single selection, `state.selectedId`, resolved via `entryIndex` first, falling back to a scan of `currentViewEntries`/`currentHighlightViewEntries` for the one case `entryIndex` can't cover — a selected row that's itself a synthetic Link pair entry (duck-types as a normal entry, never `entryIndex`-registered). Wired into `applySelection()`, the single function `selectEntry`/`selectHighlightEntry`/`revealInHighlightView` all already funnel through — every existing selection path gets a marker for free, and a plain row selection there also clears any lingering Link-view brace selection so a stale "Klammer" can't keep overriding a fresh one.

**Shown during the Link view too** (previously hidden outright): pair entries duck-type as normal entries (`.ts`/`.level` — see "Link filter" above), so `renderTimelineMinimap` works on them completely unchanged; `renderLinkView` feeds it every pair's *flattened* real entries (`getTupleEntries`, concatenated across all pairs) rather than the pair objects themselves, both for the overlay-bar density and so `updateMinimapFullRange`'s min/max covers matched (target-side) entries that can fall outside their reference entries' own span.

**Draft window** and the **right-click / long-press → time-range dialog** are covered above and in "Time filters" — both always operate on the Filtered view/tree, unaffected by which fh tab happens to be showing. Click-to-jump (plain click, no drag) selects the nearest entry in time via `lowerBoundByTs`, same "select + scroll + flash" path a row double-click uses — and, **as of this session**, resolves against whichever pane is actually visible, the same `fhLayout`/`fhActiveTab` branch `updateMinimapRenderedRange` uses: Context tab active → `currentHighlightViewEntries` + `selectHighlightEntry` (not gated on `minimapInteractive`, same reasoning as that function); otherwise → `currentViewEntries` + `selectEntry`, gated on `minimapInteractive` as before. Previously this always resolved against `currentViewEntries`/`selectEntry` regardless of which tab was showing, so a click while the Context tab was active silently jumped the (invisible) Filtered view in the background instead of the view actually on screen.

## Time context filter: window around reference entries

Built for the "show me everything that happened around this event" use case — deliberately simpler than the link filter it's modeled on. `getEntries` for a `context` node takes its parent-chain result as reference entries, builds a `[ts - contextBefore, ts + contextAfter]` window (both in ms) around each one, merges overlapping/touching windows into a sorted, non-overlapping range list (`mergeContextRanges` — an interval merge; this is the one deliberate answer to "what happens when two references' windows overlap": they become one group rather than staying as separate, duplicate-prone groups), then binary-searches (`lowerBoundByTs`/`upperBoundByTs`) the **whole root file** for entries inside those ranges (`contextWindowEntries`, shared with `countContext`: the located index spans are copied out in order — ranges are sorted and disjoint and a binary search is monotone, so each entry appears once in file order, no id Set needed). Unlike `link`, the result is **real entries from the file**, not synthetic pair objects — so any filter can be nested underneath a `context` node exactly like under any other filter, and a reference entry's own row shows up at its normal chronological position (it's always inside its own window) rather than needing a special anchor-row construct.

`node._contextRanges` (the merged range list) and `node._anchorIds` (the set of reference entry ids) are produced by `evaluateFilterCondition` (its `meta` argument; a baked `context` side computes none of it), copied onto the node by `getEntriesUncached` together with `node._cache`, and read directly off the node by the renderer — they're not separately invalidated because they're only ever populated together with the cache they ride along with.

**Rendering**: the log view (not a separate view like the link pair view) draws a left-side bracket per row when the active node is a `context` filter — `contextRangeIndex()` (binary search over `_contextRanges`) tells `renderVisibleRows()` which merged group a row's timestamp falls into; a row gets `.ctx-start`/`.ctx-end` classes by comparing against its *actual* neighbors in `currentViewEntries` (not just the virtualized render window), so the rounded bracket caps land correctly regardless of scroll position. Reference entries get a small accent dot (`.ctx-anchor-dot`). Brackets are suppressed under an active column sort (`state.sortColumn`), since sorting would scatter a group's rows apart and the bracket would stop meaning anything.

**Creating one**: **temporarily unreachable** (this session, project-owner-confirmed, FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #79) — there is currently no user-facing way to create a fresh `context` node, neither the tree's right-click menu (its "Time context…" item was removed) nor the Files & Filters sidebar toolbar (never had one beyond an initial, since-reverted pass — see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "`#sidebarToolbar`"). `#contextDialog` (a small before/after-in-milliseconds form, mirroring `#linkDialog`'s structure but needing no target-filter picker since the target is always the root file) and `openContextDialog(nodeId)` still exist and work exactly as before — they're just not wired to any button any more. **Existing `context` nodes are entirely unaffected**: one from an old session, a saved filter file, or a library preset still loads, renders, evaluates, and can be renamed/deleted/copied/cut/inverted-excluded exactly as documented above. FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #79 has the reasoning (a possible lighter, view-level replacement) and is where a future creation entry point would land.

This is the intended way to pull values from *both* sides of a pair into one extraction-table row.

## Count context filter: fixed number of entries around reference entries

A sibling of the Time context filter above (`filterType: "countContext"`, fields `countBefore`/`countAfter`), added this session (person-requested: *"Analog zum Time Context erstelle einen Count Context, bei dem man einfach die Anzahl der Log Einträge vor und/oder nach dem Anchor einstellen kann. Also anstatt eines Zeitfensters, eine feste Anzahl an Logeinträgen davor oder danach."*) — same "show me everything around this event" use case, but windows by a fixed **number of entries** instead of a time span, for logs whose entry density varies too much for a millisecond window to reliably capture "N entries of context" (a burst of activity vs. a quiet stretch).

`getEntries`'s `countContext` branch looks up each reference entry's own index in the root file's `entries` array (`buildOrderIndexMap`, the same helper the `link` filter's tie-break already uses) and builds an inclusive `[idx - countBefore, idx + countAfter]` **index** window per reference, clamped to `[0, pool.length - 1]`. `mergeCountContextRanges` (the count-based counterpart of `mergeContextRanges`) merges these the same way, with one deliberate difference in the merge condition: since these are discrete integer indices rather than continuous timestamps, two windows merge when they overlap **or sit back-to-back with no gap** (`next.start <= last.end + 1`) — index 10 and index 11 are adjacent with nothing between them, so they read as one continuous bracket the same way two touching time windows already do. The actual kept entries are sliced directly from the pool by index — exact, no binary search needed since the indices are already known.

**Rendering reuses the exact same mechanism as Time context** — `node._contextRanges`/`node._anchorIds` are populated in the identical shape, and `renderVisibleRows`'s bracket/anchor-dot code now checks for `filterType === "context" || filterType === "countContext"` rather than one specific type. The one wrinkle: `contextRangeIndex()` (used by the renderer) binary-searches `_contextRanges` by **timestamp**, so a `countContext` node's index ranges are re-expressed in ts-space (`{start: pool[lo].ts, end: pool[hi].ts}`) before being stored on the node — exact for the actual filtered result (computed from real indices, never from these ts bounds), with one accepted cosmetic-only edge case: a range boundary entry that happens to share its exact timestamp with an entry just outside the window (a tie) can make the bracket render one row wider/narrower than the true index window. Same class of accepted trade-off as the Time context bracket's own tie edge cases.

**Creating one**: **temporarily unreachable**, same as Time context above and for the same reason (this session, project-owner-confirmed, FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #79) — no right-click item, no sidebar-toolbar action. `#countContextDialog` (`#contextDialog`'s structural twin — same backdrop/positioning CSS, same open/close/create wiring, "Entries before"/"Entries after" number inputs instead of milliseconds) and `openCountContextDialog(nodeId)` still exist and work exactly as before, just unreferenced by any button. **Existing `countContext` nodes are entirely unaffected** — loading, rendering, evaluation, and editing all still work exactly as documented below. Threaded through every persistence carrier the "Known gotchas" note requires: `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`, `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`, plus `FILTER_TYPES` and the tree's type tag (`CNT`, next to `CTX` for the time-based one). Inversion (NOT) is excluded for the same reason as `context` (every window always contains its own reference entry, so a parent-relative difference would always be empty) — the fourth exclusion alongside `link`/`extract`/`context`.

## Gap filter: time distance to the previous entry (`"gap"`)

`filterType: "gap"`, `value: { ms, per }` (FEATURE_BACKLOG.md #24). Keeps the entries of the **parent's result** whose time distance to the **previous entry of that result** is `>= ms`. With `per` set to a column key (Thread, Location, Method, a custom column, or `"source"` for a merged file's source files — `entryGroupValue`), the distance is measured to the previous entry **with the same value in that column** instead: one pass, a `Map` of the last ts per group (`computeGapEntries`). The first entry (of each group) has no predecessor and is never kept. Chain-aware like every filter: `"Heartbeat"` → `Gap ≥ 1.5 s` finds missed heartbeats; `Gap ≥ 2 s per Thread` on a multi-threaded log finds per-thread stalls that the plain gap to the previous line hides (somebody always logs).

- **Everything lives in `value`** (like `timerange`'s `{ from, to }`), so every persistence carrier already threads it, and `bakeNodeCondition` makes it usable as an AND/OR side (`evaluateFilterCondition`'s `"gap"` branch). No new node field. Replaced wholesale on edit (`updateGapNodeWithUndo`, generic field-edit undo).
- **Movement class**: narrowing (a subset, same shape), so Table/Plot inheritance walks through it. NOT works generically (the parent minus the kept rows). Not in `PER_ENTRY_FILTER_TYPES` — a tail append recomputes it.
- **Filtered view**: the Δt column of a gap node's rows shows the **measured gap** (per group, against the parent) instead of the distance to the previous visible row — `node._gapMs` (entry id → gap, set next to `_cache`) read by `appendLogRow`; shown under a column sort too, since it isn't row adjacency. Not on an inverted gap node. A hidden Δt column hides it. **Ranking without a threshold**: `Gap ≥ 0` (optionally per Thread) plus a click on the sortable Δt header (largest first) lists the longest pauses first — see `docs/ui-and-views.md` → "Column sort".
- **Dialog** `#gapDialog` (`openGapDialog`): "Gap ≥ [value] [ms / s / min] measured per [none / columns ▾]", the filter popup's live result summary (`renderLiveResults` into `#gapResults`, each sample row led by its gap), Create / Save. Opened from the tree context menu's **"Gap filter…"** (a new child of the right-clicked node — file or filter) and from Edit filter… / Ctrl+E / double-click on a gap node (pre-filled; `gapThresholdParts` picks the unit). Node name `Gap ≥ 2 s per Thread`, tree tag `GAP`, clock icon. Thresholds are rounded to whole ms.
- **Not done** (optional in the request): a "⏸ 31.8 s without entries" label in the Context view's gap separators.

Tested: **GROUP 289**.

## Muting a filter node

`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #14 (2026-09-29). A filter node can carry `muted: true` (absent = false): `getEntries` then returns its parent's result untouched, so the step is effectively switched off while it stays in the tree with its colour, assertions, NOT flag and children. Children keep evaluating, against the muted node's (= its parent's) result, i.e. against the nearest non-muted ancestor. A muted node is never cached on itself (the check sits before `node._cache`, one property read), and toggling goes through `toggleMuteWithUndo(ids)` -> `invalidateNodeSubtreeCaches(id)` per toggled node (its descendants' caches derive from its result), like the NOT toggle. NOT is ignored while muted and comes back on unmute.

Not mutable: file nodes and locked nodes (Bookmarks/Sources) — `isMutableNode`. Every other filter type (text, time, level, idset, gap, context, and/or, link, ...) can be muted; there is no subtree muting.

**Controls**: the tree row's eye button (`.tree-mute`, right before `.tree-del`; `stopPropagation` so the click neither selects nor opens anything), the sidebar toolbar's Mute/Unmute button (after Invert (NOT); glyph flips eye / eye-off), the tree context menu's single-node item (next to Invert) and its multi-select item, and the rebindable `muteFilter` shortcut (`M`, on the active node or on all of a 2+ multi-selection). A multi-node toggle is ONE undo step: an `edit` entry per changed node wrapped in the `batch` undo kind (the label reads `Unmute` when every mutable selected node is muted, otherwise `Mute` = mute all).

**Look**: a muted row's label is struck through in `--text-tertiary`, icon and swatch at 45% opacity, the count is italic and shows the parent's count (tooltip "Muted — passes all N entries through"), the eye stays visible in `--level-warn`.

**Where a muted node is skipped** (it is a tree-position property, not a condition): `findExtractionAncestor` continues upward past it, so a muted wildcard node does not unlock Table/Plot and assertions on it are never evaluated; `isLinkNode` is false for a muted link node, so it renders the plain entry table instead of the Link pair view; `computeHighlightMap`, `getTextMatchHighlightNodes` and `getHighlightMatchNodes` ignore it. Creating AND/OR/Link from a selection containing a muted node bakes the node's real condition (unaffected by mute); Unpack creates unmuted nodes.

**Persistence**: `muted` is written by `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree` (read by `restoreSubtree`), `captureNodeFields`/`applyNodeFields`, `serializeFilterBranch` (read by `importFilterJson`, so library presets and JSON exports keep it) and `serializeFilterTreeForCache` (read by `materializeCachedFilters`). Regression-tested: **Group 321**.

## Recent-filter suggestions

`FEATURE_BACKLOG.md` #13 (2026-09-29). A dropdown under the filter popup's input (`#filterInput`, hosted in `.filter-input-wrap`, absolutely positioned so it overlays the sections below instead of pushing layout) and under the find bar's `#findInput` lists recently used filters. Both use ONE component, `createRecentDropdown({ input, host, apply, hideOnBlur })`.

**History**: `localStorage` key `philogg.recentFilters`, an array (most recent first) of `{ value, isRegex, caseSensitive, wholeWord, inverted, source: "filter"|"find" }`, deduped on value + the four flags (`recordRecentFilter` moves a re-used entry to the top), capped at `RECENT_FILTERS_MAX` (50); `RECENT_FILTERS_SHOW` (8) are listed. Read/written with try/catch, so blocked storage only means an empty history. Recorded by `commitFilter` (Add filter and Save in edit mode; source `filter`), by the find bar's Enter and `addFindAsFilter` (source `find`, only case/regex flags) — never per keystroke; empty/whitespace values are skipped.

**Shown**: on opening the popup in create mode and the find bar, but only while the input is EMPTY at the end of the open path (header `Recent filters`; a prefill such as "Filter for this message", a selection prefill or the find bar's previous query keeps the list closed until the user types) and on every `input` (`Matching recent filters`; case-insensitive substring match, an entry equal to the input is hidden, no list without matches). Edit mode opens with the list closed until the user types. Rows: search icon for `find` entries (empty 11px slot otherwise), value in mono with the typed part in `<mark>` (accent-strong, bold), badges `.*`/`Aa`/`W`/`NOT`, hover `x` (`Remove from history`), footer hint.

**Interaction**: Up/Down move the selection (none initially); Enter or Tab with a selection applies it and does NOT commit (Enter without one is the popup's normal Add filter / the find bar's step); Escape closes the list first (the handler `stopPropagation`s so the global Escape handler doesn't also close the popup/bar), the next Escape closes those; Shift+Delete removes the selected entry. Mouse: `mousedown` (default prevented, the input keeps focus) applies; the `x` removes on `click`; the box stops click propagation and hides with the `hidden` attribute instead of emptying itself, so the global click-outside handler never sees a detached target (see the popup gotchas); clicking elsewhere in the popup/find bar closes the list, the find bar also on blur. Applying in the popup writes `#filterInput.value`, the Syntax switch, Match case, Whole word and NOT via the popup's own setters, then calls `updateFilterAvailability()` + `evaluateLiveMatch()` (programmatic writes fire no `input` event); in the find bar it sets value + Aa + `.*` and re-runs `applyFindQuery(true)`. Regression-tested: **Group 322**.

## Filter rules: the three movement classes, and Table/Plot upward-lookup inheritance

**This session (2026-09-04), person-requested**: a filter created as a child of an extraction-pattern node (a `"text"` node whose pattern has `[*:...]`/`[*]` wildcards) used to lose Table/Plot entirely, even though conceptually it should still show the (now further-filtered) extraction table/plot. Fixed by having Table/Plot look **upward** through the tree instead of only ever asking about the active node itself.

**Basic model.** Every filter node's `filterType` belongs to exactly one of three "movement classes", describing how it transforms its parent's entry set:

1. **Narrowing (Subset)** — most filter types: a plain `"text"` filter (no extraction pattern), `"timerange"`/`"after"`/`"before"`, `"idset"`, `"level"`, `"and"`/`"or"`. The result is a subset of the parent's entries, same entry *shape*.
2. **Transforming (shape change)** — a `"text"` filter WITH an extraction pattern (`nodeHasExtractableWildcards` true) and `"link"` (synthetic paired entries, see "Link filter" above). Both change what an entry conceptually *is*: an extraction node's own entries are unchanged, real log entries, but it's the node a pattern is defined on; a link node's entries are synthetic pairs with a different shape entirely.
3. **Extending (context)** — `"context"`/`"countContext"`: pull additional real entries from the root file as context around the parent's anchors. The result is a *bigger* set, but every entry in it is still a real, ordinary log entry — same shape as the parent's.

| filterType | Class |
|---|---|
| `text` (no pattern), `after`, `before`, `timerange`, `idset`, `level`, `and`, `or`, `gap` | Narrowing |
| `text` (with `[*:...]`/`[*]` pattern), `link` | Transforming |
| `context`, `countContext` | Extending |

**Derived capability — the upward-lookup rule.** Classes 1 and 3 are *transparent* for Table/Plot purposes: narrowing or extending a set doesn't change what its entries fundamentally are, so if an ancestor's entries were extractable, a narrowed/extended descendant's entries still are, using the same pattern. Class 2 is where extraction-view either **starts** (an extraction-pattern `"text"` node) or **terminates** (a `"link"` node — its paired entries no longer have the shape the ancestor's pattern was written against, and a link node itself is not extraction-view either, unchanged prior behavior).

`findExtractionAncestor(node)` implements the walk: return the node itself if `nodeHasExtractableWildcards(node)`; otherwise walk `parentId` upward, returning the first ancestor for which that's true — but stop and return `null` the moment a `"link"` node is reached (do not walk past it), and likewise `null` once the root/file node is reached with nothing found. `nodeIsExtractionView(node) = !!findExtractionAncestor(node)` is the boolean form, a drop-in replacement for `nodeHasExtractableWildcards` at every call site that gates "does this node show a Table/Plot view" (tab enablement, the Filtered-pane-vs-extraction-pane scroller pick, remembered-view restoration) — roughly a dozen call sites (`renderMainView`, `activeNavScroller`, `applyActivationView`, the tab-refresh call in `applyFhView`). Call sites about the node's **own** pattern specifically — the tree's `TBL` type tag/icon (which identifies *which* node the pattern is defined on, not whether Table/Plot is reachable) and the filter-popup editing UI — deliberately keep calling `nodeHasExtractableWildcards` directly; switching those to the inherited form would misidentify a plain narrowing child as itself carrying a pattern.

**Applying the inherited pattern.** The actual rendering path (`renderExtractTable(node)`) is not a boolean gate — it needs a real node to pull `compileExtractPattern(...)`/`ignoredColumns` from. It resolves `const patternNode = findExtractionAncestor(node) || node` once, compiles the pattern and reads `ignoredColumns` off `patternNode`, but still builds rows from `getEntries(node.id)` — the **active** node's own (already narrowed/extended) entries, not the ancestor's. A timerange filter under an extraction node therefore shows the same columns as its ancestor's table, just fewer rows. Per-node refinements that aren't part of the pattern itself — `assertions`, `columnRenames`, `plotConfig` — deliberately stay keyed to the active node rather than the ancestor, so a descendant can annotate its own (filtered) view of the table independently.

**No new persisted field.** This is a pure live lookup, computed at render time from the current tree position — nothing is threaded through `cloneSubtree`, `snapshotSubtree`/`restoreSubtree`, `serializeFilterBranch`/`importFilterJson`, or `serializeFilterTreeForCache`/`materializeCachedFilters`; they already work correctly unmodified since a node's `filterType`/`value`/`parentId` (everything the walk needs) already round-trip through all four. Moving or pasting a node elsewhere in the tree silently changes whether it inherits Table/Plot — no visual hint calls this out (an open design question during this session's planning, explicitly decided **not** needed).

**Known non-cases**: a filter directly under a `"link"` node never inherits, even if a real extraction-pattern node sits further up past the link (the walk stops at the link, it does not skip over it). A `"link"` node's own children start a fresh walk from the link node itself — since the link node is not extraction-view, neither is anything under it unless a *new* extraction-pattern node is created there.

**When adding a new `filterType`**, two questions decide how it interacts with this model: (1) which movement class does it belong to — does it narrow, transform the shape, or extend with same-shape entries — and (2) if it's a shape-transforming type like `link`, should the upward walk stop at it (as `link` does), or is its own result still extractable in principle? Getting this wrong either silently breaks inheritance for a type that should be transparent, or silently lets Table/Plot "float" a pattern across a shape boundary it shouldn't cross.

Regression-tested: **Group 173** — a timerange filter under an extraction-pattern node inherits `nodeIsExtractionView`/reachable Table tab, with `renderExtractTable` applying the ancestor's pattern to the child's own narrowed entries (fewer rows, same columns); a filter under a `"link"` node does not inherit even conceptually past it; a plain narrowing chain with no extraction-pattern ancestor anywhere stays non-extraction-view (regression baseline).
